author: mahrud
title: Memory intensive module
note: Stands, and the question mahrud actually asked has never been answered. Not reproducible here -- the input is a 95MB external file that only he has, so this is a foreign repro. What can be established. Some of the work mikestillman offered in the thread landed: rawMatrixReadMsolveString and rawMatrixReadMsolveFile now exist at d/interface.dd:2097 and :2114, with e/BasicPolyListParser.hpp behind them and a unit test at e/unit-tests/MatrixIOTest.cpp. But they are wired only into the Msolve package (Msolve.m2:31 and :106) for reading msolve output, so there is still no general facility for loading a large matrix from a file, which is what the issue is about. His two follow-up questions are both unanswered: "why would loading a large matrix from memory require more memory than when it was defined" (2024-08-07) and "is there a way to print a sparse matrix" (2025-04-21). The stack trace is 9000 frames of binding_bind in d/binding.d, i.e. the parser recursing over the literal, which supports his own suspicion that the cost is in turning the text into a matrix rather than in reading the file. His zget suggestion for gzipped input is a separate wish nobody took up.

author: antonleykin
title: `isHomogeneous` incorrect for a Weyl algebra
note: Reproduces exactly: isHomogeneous W1 is true on 1.26.06-40 where it should be false, for W1 = QQ[x,dx,WeylAlgebra=>{x=>dx}] with default degrees. antonleykin identified the cause in the body and it is unchanged -- isHomogeneous PolynomialRing := R -> true in m2/polyrings.m2 returns true unconditionally, so a Weyl algebra whose relations are not homogeneous for its degrees is reported homogeneous anyway. The element-level tests are correct in both directions (isHomogeneous 0_W1 false, isHomogeneous 0_W2 true), so it is the ring-level predicate alone. mahrud proposed making WeylAlgebra its own type inheriting from EngineRing or QuotientRing, with the caveat that the motivation for keeping it a PolynomialRing was mixing variable kinds; nobody replied. Labels: WeylAlgebras already there.

author: mahrud
title: reduce breaks algorithms
note: Stands as a live design question, and the most recent word on it is two months old. Doug said "Yikes! I will revert the changes from #3013" and then did not -- mahrud talked him out of it in the next comment, and PR #3013 "Use reduce when adding/subtracting/negating matrices" is still merged and in force: on 1.26.06-40, v + v for v = map(ZZ^1/ideal 2, ZZ^1, 1) returns 0, the reduced answer, not the | 2 | of 1.22. The ReduceHooks machinery mahrud disables in his init.m2 is at m2/matrix.m2:88-94, with the Default hook still rawF % raw gb presentation tar. His 2026-06-15 comment is current: of the four spellings, map(coker(2*id_(ZZ^2)), , matrix{{3},{3}}) gives | 3 | while map with an explicit source, or with a list instead of a matrix, all give | 1 |. So the inconsistency is not just slow-versus-fast, it is that the same map has two answers depending on how it is spelled. Five options were tabled (mahrud), jkyang92 and mikestillman weighed in, mikestillman recalled that he and DanGrayson deliberately reduce for multiplication and not for addition, and no decision was ever recorded. Performance not re-measured here: the FGLM cyclic(7) example is the one that timed out in batch 51 on a different row, and the row does not turn on the exact figure.

author: mahrud
title: Symbol as Optional Argument
note: Stands: bare symbols are still not accepted as options. On 1.26.06-40, g = method(Options => {Verbose => false}) then g(1, Verbose) errors "no method found for applying g to: argument 1 : 1 (of class ZZ), argument 2 : Verbose (of class Symbol)". Nothing was implemented. pzinn objection in the thread is the open question and mahrud answer to it was a proposal rather than a decision: what happens to a function that takes a Symbol as a genuine non-optional argument, with mahrud suggesting such functions take a list of symbols instead, or that method gain an option to disable the behaviour. Nobody has ruled. Type Feature was already right. #4545 shares vocabulary only.

author: d-torrance
title: Inconsistent behavior when dividing by zero in integer/polynomial division
note: Reproduces byte-for-byte, all seven lines, on 1.26.06-40: 1 // 0 gives 0, 1 % 0 gives 1, quotientRemainder(1, 0) gives (0, 1), while over ZZ[x] both 1_R // 0_R and 1_R % 0_R error "cannot use division algorithm dividing by zero" and quotientRemainder(1_R, 0_R) still returns (0, 1). So the inconsistency is on two axes at once, integer versus polynomial and quotientRemainder versus the operators it is supposed to package, and neither has moved. Doug own PR #3062 attempted the fix and was blocked by InvariantRing depending on the current behaviour; the design question he ends on -- whether division by zero should be allowed at all in the polynomial case, or at minimum whether //, % and quotientRemainder should agree -- has had no answer in over two years and no comments. Adjacent rows on the same operators: #2786 (division over RR and CC, triaged in batch 49) and #1711.

author: mahrud
title: Problem with ^1 and ^**1
note: Reproduces exactly on 1.26.06-40, both halves: for M = R^{-2} ++ R^{2}, components M and components M^2 each give two summands while components M^1 gives the single {R^2}, and (set {1,2})^**1 still gives set {1 : (1), 1 : (2)} rather than the set itself. Deliberately NOT filed as a duplicate: pzinn identified it as another instance of #2891 and mahrud agreed but asked to keep it open because the ^1 and ^**1 case is much easier to resolve than the general direct sum one, so the reporter has already ruled on the question. #2891 is triaged separately in this sweep and stays open too. The cached-resolution half of the body -- M.cache.?resolution true but (M^1).cache.?resolution false -- is the same loss of cached information seen from another angle.

author: mahrud
title: Homogeneity bug in basis(..., SourceRing => ...)
note: Reproduces exactly on 1.26.06-40: with R = reesAlgebra trim monomialCurveIdeal(S, {2,3,5,6}) over ZZ/101[x_0..x_4], B = basis(1, R^1, SourceRing => S) has isHomogeneous B false, source basis(1, R^1) is R^7 with degrees {3:{1,2}, 4:{1,3}}, and source B is S^7 with all degrees zero -- exactly the target-fine, source-wrong split mahrud describes. This row already carries a comment from this project, posted 2026-08-12 in the bugs/ phase under the marker bug-triage:bugs/mike/1-integralClosureIdeal.m2, which adds the second consequence of the same phi: with no way to supply the map and no check that one exists, SourceRing silently accepts an unrelated ring and stores a RingMap that sends everything to zero, and the TODO directly above basis.m2:249-252 already describes that case. So nothing further is owed here. mahrud second comment, showing rawIsHomogeneous returning false even when DegreeMap and DegreeLift are given explicitly, is unanswered by mikestillman. #2580 shares vocabulary and is a different ask.

author: mahrud
title: isMutable MutableMatrix
note: Reproduces exactly on 1.26.06-40: isMutable mutableMatrix {{1}} is false, same as isMutable matrix {{1}}, and ancestors MutableMatrix is still {MutableMatrix, HashTable, Thing}. Control confirming the predicate itself works: isMutable new MutableHashTable is true. So mahrud diagnosis in the body is the whole of it -- MutableMatrix inherits from HashTable rather than MutableHashTable, and isMutable keys off the ancestry. His proposed fix, reparenting to MutableHashTable, has had no reply in over two years. Zero comments. Adjacent rows on the same type: #944, #2741, #4376.

author: mikestillman
title: tower of exterior algebras has incorrect multiplication!
note: Reproduces exactly on 1.26.06-40, all three assertions: for R = QQ[x_1..x_3, SkewCommutative=>true] and S = R[y_1..y_4, SkewCommutative=>true], x_1*y_2 prints as -x_1*y_2, leadCoefficient leadCoefficient(x_1*y_2) is -1 where mikestillman says it should be 1, and y_2*x_1 == x_1*y_2 is false where the variables of R and S should commute. A wrong-answer bug in a tower of exterior algebras, silent -- no error, just a sign -- and with zero comments in two and a half years. #4617 "The documented commutation rule for exterior algebras" is adjacent and is about documentation rather than about the arithmetic being wrong.

author: mahrud
title: Case (in)sensitive files in macOS
note: Stands, third-party confirmed, and not testable here -- macOS, and this is Linux, so nothing I run is evidence. The record is what settles it: mahrud asked Devlin-Mallory on 2025-05-11 to retest after PR #3741 "needs and needsPackage updates" (merged 2025-05-10), giving a concrete recipe, and Devlin-Mallory replied the same day "This does appear to still be an issue". So the most recent evidence is a fresh negative result from someone on the platform, after the change that might have fixed it. mikestillman said in 2024 it would be nice to implement and that C++17 should make the information available, against DanGrayson earlier "there is no way to tell"; mahrud counter is that the filesystem does report the true capitalization, and mikestillman own ls example shows the subtlety. Related but broader, and open: #4305 "name conflicts with the packages directory files" (mikestillman, 2026-05-15) is about ANY current-directory file shadowing a packages/ file, of which macOS case-insensitivity is called out there as making it "even worse" -- a superset of this row, not a duplicate of it. Also cross-referenced: #2413 and #1108, both closed.

author: pzinn
title: coefficients not returning coefficients in the coefficient ring
note: Reproduces exactly on 1.26.06-40, and the asymmetry pzinn points at in his third comment is the sharpest way to state it: for R = QQ[a..f], S = R[x,y] and F = a*x^2+b*x*y+c*y^2, ring last coefficients F is S while ring leadCoefficient F is R. Same polynomial, same notion of coefficient, two different rings. His AssociativeAlgebras example is the practical cost -- (last coefficients(1/3*x))_(0,0) lands in the free algebra R rather than QQ, so denominator on it has no method. mikestillman gave the counter-argument in 2024-06 and it is the only thing standing in the way: coefficients can return values in the current ring when the Variables option is used, and returning matrices over different rings in the two cases was once considered bad -- while adding that without that option he almost always has to lift anyway. Nobody has ruled since. #3950 (coefficients over FreeAlgebraQuotient) and #2490 (coefficients in iterated rings) are adjacent rows in this corpus.

author: mahrud
title: Pushforward fails for the cuspidal cubic immersion
note: Reproduces exactly on 1.26.06-40: pushForward_f S^{2} for f = inducedMap map(toricProjectiveSpace 2, toricProjectiveSpace 1, matrix{{-2},{1}}) still errors "not implemented yet: unexpected degree map of ring map", from m2/pushforward.m2:147-151. The map is confirmed as described -- it sends the three variables to x_0*x_1^2, x_0^3, x_1^3, all of degree 3, with both source and target standard graded -- so mahrud question "what is this check for?" is a fair one and has never been answered by either person he asked. pzinn asked what happens if the check is removed and mahrud answered: an inhomogeneous answer. That is the useful part of the thread and it means the guard is catching something real rather than being merely conservative, so removing it is not the fix. #3284 is adjacent.

author: mahrud
title: LengthLimit in Complexes
note: Reproduces on the reference build AND on origin/development, both problems. freeResolution R^1 for R = QQ[x,y]/(x-y) still errors "need to provide LengthLimit for free resolutions over quotients of polynomial rings" even though the input is free, and freeResolution(coker vars R, LengthLimit => infinity) gives the same error even though the option IS provided. The guard is Complexes/FreeResolution.m2:138-155 in resolutionObjectInEngine: when opts.LengthLimit === infinity it errors for skew-commutative rings (:145) and for any ring whose flattening has a nonzero ideal (:152), and there is no isFreeModule short-circuit anywhere in that file. mikestillman said on 2026-06-01 that free modules "are now handled correctly (or will be with the next PR)" and that quotient and exterior cases would warn rather than error; three months on, neither is in development and I could find no open PR, so his parenthetical is still the operative half. Cross-referenced #3656 "Reporting infinite projective dimension" is adjacent, not a duplicate. mahrud last comment (2025-05-26) raises a separate symptom -- a partially computed resolution seeming stuck in an interrupted state, so that adding LengthLimit => 5 does not help while rebuilding the ideal does -- which nobody has answered.

author: d-torrance
title: RInterface test failures on loong64/riscv64 architectures
note: Stands, and n/a-platform: loong64 and riscv64, and this is x86-64, so nothing I can run is evidence. Settled on the record instead. Doug reported it on the Debian 1.23 build for loong64 and confirmed the same failure on riscv64 the next day; the symptom is that complex numbers come back as garbage -- 4.63557e-310*ii where 2+3*ii was expected, in three separate RInterface tests -- which is the signature of a struct being read at the wrong offset or width rather than of anything R-specific. His own diagnosis in the body, that the underlying issue is probably in ForeignFunctions and how structs work on this architecture, is the only one offered and nobody has replied in over two years. Worth knowing when this is picked up: the reference build carries Debian packaging patches that skip tests by architecture and this issue number is among those named, so a passing check here would say nothing either.

author: griffin-has-questions
title: Polyhedra Package Changes Lineality Space of Fan
note: Reproduces reliably, and the bug is not in fan at all: linealitySpace of a Cone is not a function of the Cone. Measured, two cones from identical H-data differing only in that the second has had rays computed: image linealitySpace A != image linealitySpace B, both of rank 8, so two different 8-dimensional subspaces of ZZ^10 and one is wrong. fan Cone (core/fan/constructors.m2:119-123) computes raysC := rays C before linealityC := linealitySpace C, so a fan always carries the rays-first answer while a freshly built cone gives the other -- which is the reported inequality, and which reframes the reporter "in some rare instances" as session state rather than rare input. Confirmed with a clean A/B on the same two fresh cones: image linealitySpace(fan C1) == image linealitySpace C2 is false; identical but with C1 == C2 evaluated first it is true, because == forces rays. Three fresh sessions gave false 3/3 on the reported expression. Near miss worth recording: my first rerun rewrote the expression to reuse one cone object and returned TRUE -- the "reusing one input across variants measures the cache" trap -- and I was one step from filing this as fixed. Locus for a fix: compute#Cone#computedLinealityBasis (core/cone/properties.m2:186) branches between three computations on whichever properties are cached when first called. One hypothesis tested and REFUTED: it is not the facets/hyperplanes versus inequalities/equations branch, since orthogonalComplement of each gives the same image here.

author: mahrud
title: equality of ideals over different rings
note: Reproduces exactly, both lines: "ideal 0 == 0 * ideal vars(QQ[x])" and "ideal 1 == ideal 1_(QQ[y])" each error "expected ideals for the same ring" on 1.26.06-40. The ask is a small, well-specified behaviour change -- return false for ideals over different rings rather than erroring, except when one side is over ZZ, where Ideal == ZZ should apply -- and it has had no reply of any kind in over two years. Zero comments. #4267 (equality of visible lists) and #4461 share the word equality and nothing else.

author: mahrud
title: Better list comprehension
note: Stands: nothing was implemented, and the thread is a live design disagreement rather than a dormant request. mahrud wants set-builder syntax; Doug pointed at f \\ L and L / f; mahrud countered that compactness is not the problem and gave a concrete defect -- max({1,2,3} / i -> 10*i) errors "expected parenthesized argument list or symbol" -- which still fails today; Doug agreed the obstacle is that -> has very low precedence and that the natural operators for set-builder notation, : and |, are already taken at higher precedence; mikestillman said he personally prefers L/f to Python-style comprehensions and suggested improving those instead. mahrud last comment (2024-04-22) narrows to something concrete that could be done first: making "for x in splice(1..5,3,2:2) if odd x then x^2" work, i.e. an if without else in a for-list, tied to #1978. That specific sub-ask is the actionable residue and nobody responded to it. Type Feature was already right.

author: mahrud
title: Operator wishlist
note: Stands, and one of the three has a recorded reason it cannot be done as asked. R_+ is still a syntax error, so S_+ for the positively graded part is unimplemented. For f^#, d/binding.d:367-369 carries the attempt, commented out, with the obstacle written above it: "-- TODO: cant work because of instances like R^#m", then --export PowerSharpS := makeKeyword(postfix("^#")) and --export UnderscoreSharpS := makeKeyword(postfix("_#")). That is exactly the ambiguity mahrud anticipated in the body ("we need to be careful so x^#L still works"), already hit and already documented, so his caveat is not hypothetical. The sibling postfix operators from the PRs he had already landed -- #3183 "New operators" and #3193 "New operator for restriction" -- ARE present as ExclamationS, PowerExclamationS and UnderscoreExclamationS at binding.d:363-365, so the pattern works and it is ^# specifically that collides. The <v,u> inner product ask needs < and > to stop being binary-only; mahrud own 2024-10 comment to Doug raises the ambiguity himself (whether x < 2 , 3 > y is two comparisons or one bracket) and got no reply. Type Feature was already right.

author: mahrud
title: Add assertLevel and automatic timer
note: Stands: assertLevel is still an unbound Symbol on 1.26.06-40, and assert is still a function rather than a keyword. Nothing was implemented. The thread is a design conversation that ran into a parser problem and stopped: mahrud wants assert_n with a threshold, Doug pointed out that if assert becomes a keyword then assert_n is a syntax error and that making assert_ a keyword may not parse since _ is not usually allowed in words, and mahrud conceded, floating assert/assert1 or just two levels keyed on debugLevel instead. title: quotient and modulus for non-integers are wrong
note: Reproduces unchanged, and BOTH participants agree it is wrong -- so this is a defect with a design reference attached, not an open dispute. On 1.26.06-40, 13.3 // 4.0 is 3.325 and 13.3 % 4.0 is 0, i.e. // is a synonym for / and % is identically zero, for RR, for ZZ and QQ arguments mixed with RR, and for CC (pi*ii // 3.0 gives 1.0471975511966*ii, % gives 0). The code is m2/reals.m2:213-226, cited in the body. Sequence of the thread matters here and the first reply is not the conclusion: Doug initially defended the behaviour, arguing // and % give quotient and remainder in a Euclidean domain and that fields are trivially Euclidean since x = y(xy^-1) + 0; mahrud countered that this is just / and that // and % are meant to work on domains, gave the Python contrast (13.3 % 4.0 is 1.3000000000000007) and noted the workaround costs several steps (13.3 - 4 * floor(13.3 // 4)); and Doug then wrote "Ok, I think I am convinced that it is wrong, too" and supplied Boute, "The Euclidean Definition of the Functions div and mod" (ACM) as a survey of the available definitions. author: mahrud
title: Using Intel's Math Kernel Library with M2
note: Stands, and the substance is now in comments/issues/3372.md rather than here -- the mechanism, Doug reproduction recipe, the 2014 precedent, and why cmake breaks where autotools does not. Internal-only residue. (1) The ask is not what the body says: not "where does a #define MKL_Complex16 shim belong" but "lapack.hpp must yield when something else has already declared these symbols", and the header requirement is fflas-ffpack, not M2. (2) Doug objection to my first suggested fix is right and has a root cause: M2 configure.ac uses AX_BLAS/AX_LAPACK with zero PKG_CHECK_MODULES, and M2/m4/ax_blas.m4 carries exactly one AC_SUBST, BLAS_LIBS, with no CFLAGS -- structurally, since the Fortran BLAS/LAPACK interface is header-free. So a LINALGCFLAGS would import a dependency requirement into M2 own model of linear algebra. (3) The stale CBLAS_LIBS in linbox-team fflas-ffpack macros/mkl-check.m4:32, missed by their PR #226 in 2019, is now fixed upstream by Doug own linbox-team/fflas-ffpack PR #421 (opened 2026-08-21, CBLAS_LIBS -> BLAS_LIBS, +2/-3, open). When that lands and M2 bumps past the pinned 2.5.0, autotools builds that reach MKL start defining HAVE_MKL and fail at fflas-ffpack own configure on mkl.h, so the lapack.hpp fix and an include-path story need to precede the bump. Blast radius measured 2026-08-20 in Doug container: reachable more easily than I had assumed, because ax_blas.m4:140-143 nests the generic -lblas probe inside the PhiPACK check and demands libdgemm/libsgemm, so a plain -lblas can never satisfy AX_BLAS and any box with intel-mkl but no openblas/flexiblas/atlas dev package falls through to the MKL-by-name probes at :154; libopenblas-dev installed masks it at :123. Debian does supply the missing include path through pkg-config: blas.pc rides the same alternatives link as libblas.so and resolves to mkl-sdl-lp64.pc, giving -I/usr/include/mkl -m64. (4) MY ERRORS IN THIS INVESTIGATION, recorded because both recur: I called the "see macros/mkl-check.m4" comment a dangling reference when it points into the dependency where the file exists; and I read /fflas-ffpack in Doug container -- a standalone 2.5.1 checkout with HAVE_MKL undefined, picked by find | head -1 -- and built an account of a successful MKL build on it, when the actual M2 build is 2.5.0 under BUILD/build/libraries/fflas_ffpack/build/. He asked "which directory are you looking in?" That is the "a package own source may not be the source you tested" trap one level out: I read one tree and reasoned about a build in another. (5) I also first drafted all of the above INTO this note; Doug pointed out it is comment material, which it plainly was.

title: Bizarre crash involving local symbol and computing basis in parallel
note: Reproduces, intermittently, and the symptom has hardened since the report. Needed real parallelism to see it: at the default allowableThreads (5 here) one run was clean, but with allowableThreads = 8 and the reporter own allowableThreads*2 tasks it segfaults about 1 run in 5 -- confirmed twice over two batches of runs. author: mahrud
title: memoize and options
note: Every behaviour in the thread still reproduces on 1.26.06-40, and the reason memoize cannot see options is structural: m2/remember.m2:7-14 defines memoize(Function,List) as 'x -> values#x ??= f(x)' -- a single-argument closure keyed on x, with no OptionTable anywhere in it. So pzinn's two attempts fail for two different reasons, both measured. 'g ZZ := o -> memoize(x -> ...)' recomputes on every call including repeats of the same options, because the memoize CALL is inside the option-dispatch lambda and builds a fresh cache each invocation. 'h ZZ := memoize(o -> x -> ...)' also recomputes, because the cache is keyed on o and its value is an un-memoized inner closure. His working form, memoize(o -> memoize(x -> ...)), is the only one that caches, and 'heavy' is fair. mahrud's 2025-03-11 case reproduces too: after 'f = method(); f ZZ := x -> 2*x; f = memoize f', the line 'f QQ := x -> 3*x' does nothing observable -- memoizeValues f is still empty afterwards -- and f(1_QQ) then errors in remember.m2:11 because the memoized wrapper delegates to the original method function, which has no QQ method. The same line written with '=' rather than ':=' DOES land, in the memo cache rather than the method table: remember.m2:48 'Function Thing =' special-cases a memoized function, so 'f QQ = x -> 3*x' leaves keys memoizeValues f == {QQ} and 'f QQ' returns the closure. Measured both ways. Typed Feature to match #1993 'memoize GF', also Feature; the body asks for behaviour M2 does not have. mahrud's own 'maybe this is a moot point' is the strongest thing in the thread against acting.

author: d-torrance
title: No recursion limit error for functions of one argument
note: All four behaviours reproduce on 1.26.06-40, and the answer to mahrud's unanswered 2024-09-24 question is that M2's tail-call optimization covers exactly ONE call shape: a closure of one parameter applied to an argument that does not evaluate to a Sequence. That is the else branch of applyFCC at d/evaluate.d:627-760, whose 'while true do (...)' loop at :644 increments and decrements recursionDepth around evalAllButTail and so leaves it FLAT across iterations -- no stack growth, no limit, loops forever. Every other shape increments per call and trips at 300: a sequenceCode argument goes to applyFCCS (:616, :821) which does a plain 'recursionDepth = recursionDepth + 1; eval(model.body)', and a Sequence-VALUED argument goes to applyFCS (:626, :492) which does the same. Measured, and it is the second dispatch that settles his 'how are these two different': 'g()' on a one-parameter g binds x to the empty sequence -- 'g = x -> print class x; g()' prints Sequence, while 'g(0)' prints ZZ -- so inside the body 'g x' is now applying g to a Sequence value and takes the applyFCS path. Confirmed by construction: body 'g (1:x)' hits the limit, bodies 'g x', 'g(x)' and '(g x)' all loop, and 'identity g x' hits the limit because the recursive call is no longer in tail position. So the reported symptom is correct tail-call behaviour, not a missing check -- but there IS a live defect and it is in the documentation. Macaulay2Doc/ov_debugging.m2:401-409, the recursionLimit node, says flatly 'Each time a function is called, the recursion depth is incremented by 1 ... This limit on recursion depth is a way to detect infinite loops.' Both sentences are false for the optimized shape, and that text is exactly why this reads as a bug. The recursionDepth node two blocks below (:410-427) already warns 'Tail recursion optimization may be in effect, so there the answer may not always be what you expect' -- so the fix is to carry that sentence up. Nothing anywhere in Macaulay2Doc documents the optimization itself: git grep for 'tail recursion|tail call' over the doc packages returns nothing. What is left as a genuine feature ask is mahrud's first point, that TCO does not cover the zero- and multi-parameter cases.

author: mahrud

The rendered page carries 346 author links, of which only 235 are http(s) -- the other 111 are mailto:, which ov_packages.m2:60-62 falls back to when an author gives no HomePage. Of the 235 web links, checked one at a time with a browser user-agent, 45s timeout, redirects followed: 157 load, 58 are broken, 18 answer 403 or 999 (bot-blocking, almost certainly fine in a browser, so NOT counted broken) and 2 timed out inconclusively. The 58 are 38 gone (37x404, 1x410), 10 dead at the network layer (9 with no DNS record at all -- cohenmacaulay.life, calvino.polito.it, faculty.uscupstate.edu, flash.lakeheadu.ca, homepages.warwick.ac.uk, colinalstad.com, www.sjzelenberg.com, www.dms.auburn.edu, www.stephanieyang.com -- plus faculty.fordham.edu refusing on port 80 and cornell.edu/~takhmejanov giving an empty reply), 4 with certificates that do not validate (cecas.clemson.edu, hernandez.faculty.ku.edu, witt.faculty.ku.edu, web.iitd.ac.in) and 6 with redirect faults. So 'about 60 / 340' was right on the number and wrong on the base: 58 of 235, a quarter of the testable links, undecayed in two years. ONE OF THE BROKEN LINKS IS DAN'S, in Core itself: m2/Core.m2:15 gives HomePage => 'http://www.math.uiuc.edu/~dan/', which 301s to 'https://math.illinois.edu~dan/' -- malformed, the slash is missing from the redirect -- and does not resolve. THE TOOLING GAP: Macaulay2/html-check-links/html-check-links.c is 151 lines with no socket, no curl, no getaddrinfo and no http literal in it -- local anchors only, so nothing in the tree could ever have caught an external 404. Measured today: 'linkchecker --check-extern --recursion-level=1' on this one page checked 363 links in 494 URLs and reported 69 errors in 1m47s, including the mailto entries as mail URLs; the 69 against my 58 is the 403s, which LinkChecker counts and I did not. #953 ('html-check-links program', Dan 2019, closed wontfix by this project 2026-08-16) already argued the broader question of whether a hand-rolled flex/bison checker should exist when general-purpose ones are packaged, and measured LinkChecker as the packaged alternative; it said that question deserved its own issue and NOBODY EVER FILED ONE (gh search for 'link checker' and 'linkchecker' returns only #953). DOUG'S SCOPE DECISION, 2026-08-21: the comment frames the checker as the REMEDY for this issue -- dead links are the symptom, nothing in the tree can see an external link, so a checker doing internal and external is the fix, which answers mahrud's 'should we just not link them?' with a third option he did not have. The issue is NOT widened into the broader 'should html-check-links be replaced at all' ask, so no retitle: the title still describes the live problem and the tool is the answer to it. #953 is cited only as where the tooling question was already raised. Typed Task: tracker maintenance and a policy decision about whether to link at all. mahrud's parenthetical wish for 'a sensible organization of the list' is separate and much smaller -- the sort at ov_packages.m2:67-71 is by last name via 'last separate(" ", name)'.

author: mahrud
title: Extra space in expressions of sequences
note: Reproduces on 1.26.06-40 once 'kk' is replaced by a real ring (the cached run said 'differs' at 0% because the transcript's 'R = kk[x,y]' fails -- kk is not defined in M2, so nothing after it ran): net ideal x is 'ideal x', net ideal(x+y) is 'ideal(x + y)', net ideal(x,y) is 'ideal (x, y)'. Mechanism, completing the comparison pzinn himself invited. net Adjacent (m2/expressions.m2:660-679) branches on 'precedence args > p': a Sequence argument has precedence 74 against the Adjacent's 62, so it takes :669, and the exemption list at :671 -- Array, Divide, or a multi-line netfun -- does not cover Sequence, so it falls to :673 horizontalJoin(netfun, " ", netargs). A Sum argument has precedence 50, below 62, so it takes :677 and parenthesizes itself with no separator. That asymmetry is the defect and nothing in the code intends it. texMath Adjacent (:688-690) already handles the identical case: 'instance(args,VisibleList)' gets sep="{}", zero width, which is why the WebApp output has no gap. PZINN'S 'BEWARE OF UNINTENDED CONSEQUENCES' IS THE ONLY THING IN THE WAY AND IT HAS NOW BEEN COSTED. Adding VisibleList to :671 was patched in at runtime and measured. Twelve real objects rendered before and after: ten change, each by exactly one column, with height, depth and multi-line alignment preserved -- including the two awkward ones, a stacked-exponent 'ideal (x^7 + y^7, ...)' and 'ideal (x/y, y/z)' whose fraction bars shift together. Single-generator ideals and bare cokernels are untouched. Brace renderings are untouched too, which is the part that could have gone wrong since VisibleList covers List as well as Sequence: 'set {1,2,3}' passes its argument as a Holder and cokernel and image pass a MatrixExpression, neither a VisibleList, so 'cokernel {...}' (229 output-line starts in the installed corpus), 'set {...}' (126), 'image {...}' (75) and 'triangulation {...}' (35) keep their space; Array arguments already have none. THE COMMITTED DIFF IS 36 LINES IN 14 FILES, and my first estimate was wrong in the way that mattered. 3798 output lines in 1296 of 8182 example-output files across 172 of 290 packages would change, but git ls-files finds zero example-output paths -- those are build artifacts under share/doc, regenerated on any build and invisible to version control. Only 335 .out files are tracked at all, the pre-computed ones for packages needing external software (NCAlgebra 126, Bertini 27, Tropical 25, PHCpack 23), and 14 of those carry the pattern for 36 output lines, none of them input lines. No test asserts on the spacing either: grepping tests/ and packages/ for the four affected identifiers followed by ' (' returns 34 matches, all input strings inside EXAMPLE blocks. #766 CAME UP IN THE DUPLICATE SEARCH AND IS NOT RELATED -- do not cite it. It is the space AFTER the commas ('net (1,2,3)' is '(1, 2, 3)', from the between(", ", ...) inside net of a sequence, equally visible in 'net {1,2,3}'); this is the space BEFORE the paren, from net Adjacent. Inert in both directions: the patch output is 'ideal(x, y)', paren space gone and comma space intact, and precedence Sequence (:703) is keyed on class and length, never on rendered text, so changing the separator cannot flip the branch that produces the paren space. The only link is caller/callee, net Adjacent computing netargs := net args at :665, so one rendering happens to display both spaces. Nor is the objection shared: #766 was closed on 'breaks way too many examples', about a separator appearing in every sequence and list; pzinn's remark here is a caution about net Adjacent with a pointer to texMath. I first wrote #766 up as a precedent and Doug rejected that, correctly -- this is spacing between a function and its argument list, #766 is the formatting of the arguments themselves. NOT A PR: acting on this verdict is separate work in a separate branch, per README; I drifted into proposing one and Doug pulled it back.

author: pzinn
title: More linear algebra speed issues
note: Reproduces, and all four observations in the thread hold with numbers. pzinn's matrix is not in the issue, so I built a 461x149 QQ matrix of rank 100 (product of a 461x100 and a 100x149 random dense matrix, seed 42) which gives a genuinely 49-dimensional kernel. On 1.26.06-40: kernel m 173.0s; kernel promote(m,QQ[]) 21.7s, an 8.0x gap against his reported 7.6x; reducedRowEchelonForm m 0.37s, 470x faster than kernel; nullSpace mutableMatrix m 0.35s, returning the same 149x49 answer. So his 2025-05-21 'making it a mutable matrix also solves the problem' REPRODUCES and is the cheapest route by ~500x. MY OWN FIRST TEST OF THAT WAS WRONG and would have published a false refutation: I timed 'kernel matrix mutableMatrix m', which round-trips back to an immutable Matrix and so measured nothing (224s, identical to kernel m). There is no kernel(MutableMatrix); nullSpace(MutableMatrix) is the method, alongside rank, solve and LUdecomposition. MIKE'S SPARSITY POINT IS CONFIRMED, which matters because it is the argument against just switching: a 3% dense 461x149 QQ matrix takes 3.0s for kernel against 220s for a fully dense one of the same shape, a 73x difference, so 'if it is really sparse, this code, although not optimized, will often be faster than dense code' holds as stated. mahrud's mechanism guess is right -- kernel of a Matrix goes through GaussElimComputation in e/gauss.cpp -- and his unanswered 2024-10-13 question checks out: 'I don't think we currently use eigen's sparse matrix class anywhere' is still true, the only SparseMatrix references in the engine being two commented-out typedefs at e/basic-mutable-matrices/smat.hpp:18-19 and a line in e/issues/TODO-rings-matrices. author: mahrud
title: Documentation links to types that conflict with a package name
note: Reproduces, and mahrud's own detection loop is the measurement. Re-running his 2025-05-11 one-liner ('for pkg in separate_" " version#"packages" do (L = about concatenate("^", pkg, "$"); if #L > 1 then print L)') on 1.26.06-40 gives FOUR of his five conflicts, unchanged: Points (FastMinors, NAGtypes, Points), Regularity (BGG, NoetherianOperators, Regularity), MultiplierIdeals (MultiplierIdeals, MultiplierIdealsDim2) and Complexes (Complexes, ReactionNetworks). THE FIFTH IS RESOLVED: his 'with Divisor being settled soon' came true -- PR #3803 'Rename Divisor package to WeilDivisors' merged 2025-07-04 by mahrud -- so the body's own SpaceCurves/Divisor example no longer misfires, while the four he listed as 'the other instances' are all still live. His stated next step is also unfulfilled: tests/normal/release-checklist.m2 exists and checks Keywords, DebuggingMode, Reload, headline style and missing package descriptions, but does NOT carry the ambiguity test he proposed. It is 'scan(prepend("Macaulay2Doc", loadedPackages), ...)' -- so the search order is Macaulay2Doc, then loaded packages in load order, and currentPackage is nowhere in it, which is exactly the fix he suggested. The warning itself fires one level up at :216, in fixup DocumentTag, where the found tag wins and is returned. THIS IS WHAT BLOCKS #3533 IN THIS SAME BATCH: Doug's draft PR #4375 adding GitHub problem matchers stalled because 'all the ambiguous reference warnings are getting flagged as errors', and :216 is the only site that emits that string. Neither issue mentions the other. Also in-tree acknowledgement at Macaulay2Doc/ov_developers.m2:12: 'FIXME: this causes warning: ambiguous reference "User :: User" and "Macaulay2Doc :: User"'. author: mahrud
title: rank fails over ZZ because codim needs Generic => true
note: Reproduces on 1.26.06-40, unchanged: 'R = ZZ[x]; rank coker vars R' still gives 'codim: expected an affine ring (consider Generic=>true to work over QQ)'. This row already carries a comment from this project (2026-08-06, from the bugs/ directory sweep), which established that dim reaches the same error by a second route and tied it to bugs/dan/1-dim from 2011, attributed there to Bart Snapp. Nothing to add to that and no second comment proposed. The state of the thread: mahrud diagnosed the plumbing gap (no way to pass Generic => true through rank -- options rank is null and every method of rank has null options), and mikestillman's 2025-05-14 reply reframed it as a capability request, 'It would be nice to have an honest rank function for modules in polynomial rings over ZZ'. author: mahrud
title: Bug in isVeryAmple for simplicial normal toric varieties
note: Reproduces byte-for-byte on 1.26.06-40: isEffective D is false, vertices D is null, and isVeryAmple D dies with 'no method found for applying numColumns to: null (of class Nothing)' at NormalToricVarieties/Divisors.m2:495, exactly the trace mahrud posted. THE FIX IS IN PR #3582, which is what his 2024-12-27 'Well I have the fix, but nobody is reviewing the pull requests' meant: 'Improvements to Simplicial Toric Varieties', opened 2024-11-15, open and not a draft, 21 commits, +248/-48 across 11 files, last touched 2026-06-07. author: mahrud
title: makeSimplicial in NormalToricVarieties occasionally makes the variety incomplete
note: Reproduces at the reported rate. mahrud saw 15 failures in 100 trials; 20 trials here gave 3, so 15% against his 15%, on 1.26.06-40 with the Bruns-Gubeladze Example 5.1 polytope. 13.7s for the 20. GGSMITH'S WORKAROUND CHECKS OUT AND THE COST IS THE REASON IT IS NOT THE ANSWER: one makeSimplicial(X, Strategy => 1) took 16.9s and returned a complete variety, against 0.59s for the default strategy on the same input, which returned an incomplete one -- a 29x price on that trial. For example, one could easily imagine that the random weight w insufficiently random' and later 'I wouldn't be surprised if the random weight vector used in Strategy => 0 could be improved; remarkably little experimentation went into its selection'; mahrud replied he had no suggestions and just reruns until it works. The 2025-05-14 exchange settles the side question rather than the bug: mahrud asked whether the desingularisation of a projective variety should stay projective, and ggsmith confirmed both strategies should preserve it, 'for the zeroth strategy, a regular triangulation of a polytope is a polytope. For the first strategy, blowups are projective morphisms.' author: mahrud
title: basis strategy and order for toric varieties
note: Stands, and it splits cleanly into a part that happened and a part that did not. WHAT EXISTS: rawHilbertBasis is wired to libnormaliz (e/interface/cone.cpp:69, exposed at d/interface.dd:3944-3947) and Polyhedra uses it, hilbertBasis calling it at core/cone/properties.m2:181 with the comment 'calls libnormaliz'; and basis' exists in Truncations at :346, 'basis' = method(Options => options basis)', which is the without-toric-assumptions implementation the body describes. WHAT DID NOT: the engine is untouched. git grep for normaliz or hilbertbasis over e/matrix-kbasis.cpp returns nothing, so basis0_multi_graded is unchanged and mahrud's second question -- 'should this be implemented in the top level, or is it worth changing basis0_multi_graded in matrix-kbasis.cpp to directly use Normaliz via rawHilbertBasis' -- has neither been answered nor acted on. His first question, addressed to mikestillman, is likewise unanswered: whether a different monomial order from the engine algorithm is a problem. Zero comments in twenty-one months. THE TOP-LEVEL HALF IS ALSO PARTLY IN PR #3582, the same unreviewed PR that carries #3575's fix and #3578's workaround: its description lists 'added support for partial multidegrees in basis'', 'added test for basis'', 'fixed a couple of bugs in basis'' and 'fixed minor bug in basis with torsion degrees'. So three rows in this batch are waiting on one PR that has been open since November 2024. #2810, which mahrud cites as the order problem he ran into, is still open. Typed Feature: this asks for an optimisation that does not exist, and the engine question is a design decision rather than a defect. author: mahrud
title: bug in rawSelectByDegrees depending on internal degrees
note: Reproduces exactly, and mahrud's minimal example is the cleanest statement of it. On 1.26.06-40 with R = QQ[x, y, Degrees => map(ZZ^1 ++ ZZ^1/ideal 3, , id_(ZZ^2))] and C = res((ideal vars R)^3): positions(degrees source C.dd_1, d -> d == {0,0}) gives {3}, rawSelectByDegrees(raw source C.dd_1, {0,0}, {0,0}) gives {} -- wrong -- and the same call on R^(-degrees source C.dd_1) gives {3} -- right. So two free modules with identical degree lists answer differently, which is the whole complaint. mikestillman's 2025-04-30 diagnosis is the mechanism and nothing has changed since: the engine's internal degree monomial for source mingens I carries a factor that is zero modulo the torsion part of the grading, and the engine does not know those degrees should be equal. NOT A DUPLICATE OF #1925, and I checked this carefully because #1925 is older and getting it backwards would close the survivor. #1925 (mahrud, 2021, open, commented by this project on 2026-08-19) is about rawSelectByDegrees given MALFORMED or partial degree arguments -- degreeLength is 3 there and the argument is {1} -- returning nondeterministic garbage with no error. This row is well-formed arguments over a torsion grading returning a wrong answer. Different cause, same function; mahrud himself wrote 'Related: #1925' rather than claiming a duplicate. THE WORKAROUND IS ALREADY WRITTEN, in the unreviewed PR #3582, and it is exactly the M-versus-N distinction from the report: 'selectByDegrees = (M, lo, hi) -> rawSelectByDegrees(raw (ring M)^(-degrees M), lo, hi)', carrying the comment '-- c.f. https://github.com/Macaulay2/M2/issues/3578'. So rebuilding the free module from its own degree list is a reliable dodge, and it is sitting unmerged. Engine label already present and correct. The slowness half of the report -- degrees M taking seconds -- I did not reproduce; it needs the full toric example rather than the minimal one, and mahrud said himself the torsion explanation does not cover it.

author: mahrud
title: bug in basis of zero modules
note: Reproduces on 1.26.06-40, and the cached run's 'same-output at 100%' is accurate: basis image(0 * matrix id_(QQ^2)) still returns the 2x2 identity, while the same construction over QQ[x] returns 0. Returning a basis of the zero module that is not zero is the defect. mikestillman located it on 2025-04-29 and the code is unchanged: e/matrix-kbasis.cpp around :477, 'const PolynomialRing *P = bottom->get_ring()->cast_to_PolynomialRing(); if (P == nullptr) return Matrix::identity(bottom->rows());' -- so any non-polynomial ring gets an identity matrix regardless of the module. His own reaction is worth preserving: 'I have no idea why we/I thought this was a good way to handle that. Uugh!' THE THREAD IS SPLIT ON THE REMEDY, three ways, and that is why it is still open. Mike proposed erroring when the input is not a polynomial ring or a quotient of one. mahrud replied 'I'd rather it worked than give an error, but I don't care if it's handled in the engine or top level.' n-m-g on 2025-05-24 argued basis is the wrong tool for this and gens image f is the idiomatic route, siding with the error. So the disagreement is whether basis over a field should compute a vector-space basis or refuse, and nobody has decided. Typed Bug: whatever the answer, an identity matrix for a zero module is wrong. Labelled Engine, since the line is in matrix-kbasis.cpp and both proposed fixes touch it or guard it.

author: mahrud
title: keyword `in` or `∈` for membership checking
note: Stands, and the confusing part is that the symbols exist while neither thing asked for does. m2/exports.m2:1329-1331 carries the Unicode synonym table entries '∀' => 'all', '∃' => 'any', '∈' => 'isMember'. Those are aliases for FUNCTION NAMES, so on 1.26.06-40 the prefix forms work -- ∈(1, {1,2}) is true, ∀({1,2}, i -> i > 0) is true -- and that is precisely the state pzinn's 2024-12-02 comment complains about: 'already synonyms, but for which the current syntax doesn't match proper mathematical conventions'. Neither half of mahrud's request works. Infix membership: '1 ∈ {1,2}' fails with 'no method found for applying isMember to: {1, 2}', because the alias makes it adjacent application of isMember to the right operand rather than a binary operator. And '1 in {1,2}' outside a for clause is a parse error, 'syntax error at in'. Nor does 'for x ∈ {1,2} do ...' work: ∈ is not a synonym for the keyword in, so it parses as something else and dies. A BINARY ∈ DOES EXIST, BUT NOT HERE: pzinn's 7512ea59c8 'new binary method ∈' (2023-08-23) and d867ddd0eb 'various fixes/deforks; member symbol removed for now' (2024-02-22) are both on his fork and neither is an ancestor of origin/development, so the work has been written and never landed. Typed Feature was already correct. Labelled Interpreter: making ∈ a synonym for the in keyword, and giving in a meaning outside for, are both parser changes in binding.d rather than Core script changes.

author: pzinn
title: User-created keywords
note: Reproduces on 1.26.06-40: getSymbol "⊗" returns a Keyword, and class of it is Keyword, so pzinn's second observation stands unchanged. THE WORK EXISTS AS AN OPEN PR AND IS THE largest thing in this batch: PR #3599 'User-defined keywords', pzinn's own, opened 2024-12-01, still open and NOT a draft, +268/-262 across 18 files, last updated 2025-09-01. So his closing 'I intend to rewrite binding.d and actors5.d which have become a mess' became a real submission that has sat for a year. Its review thread is substantive rather than stalled on nothing: mahrud pushed on terminology -- that Symbol and Keyword are identical except for parsing, so the naming should reflect that -- pzinn agreed, and asked for a common ancestor rather than two identical methods makeKeyword and makeOperator; mahrud's position is that makeKeyword should not exist at all 'since by definition keywords are the preserved symbols'. That vocabulary question is unresolved and is what the PR is waiting on. pzinn's own 2024-11-27 analysis is the mechanism and is worth keeping: at the d level Keyword and Symbol are both SymbolClosure, and classes.dd decides which on the fly from parsing information -- 'if s.symbol.word.parse == parseWORD then symbolClass else keywordClass'. He also notes two defects in passing that nobody has picked up: 'new Keyword from xxx' produces a SpecialExpr and probably should error, and a getSymbol-created keyword calls the dummy binary function whose err_error appears to do nothing, so it silently succeeds instead of erroring -- which is why 'a⊗b' produces no output after getSymbol "⊗". Typed Feature: this asks for a capability, and the incidental defects are consequences of its absence rather than the subject.

author: mahrud
title: genericMatrix should be row major
note: Reproduces on 1.26.06-40, unchanged: genericMatrix(R, 2, 5) over QQ[x_(1,1)..x_(2,5)] still fills column-major, so row 1 reads x_(1,1) x_(1,3) x_(1,5) x_(2,2) x_(2,4), and 'options genericMatrix' is null -- no RowMajor option was ever added, and git grep finds no genericMatrix' in the tree either. So both remedies floated in the thread are absent. THE DISCUSSION IS A GENUINE STANDOFF rather than neglect, and that is the useful thing to record. Everyone agrees the current behaviour is wrong to read: mahrud filed it from a workshop remark, Doug said it had been bugging him too and noted that Permanents already works around it with 'transpose genericMatrix(R1,xxX_(1,1),c,r)', pzinn said it annoyed him twenty years ago. What blocks it is mikestillman: 'I agree that the proposed way is better, but I'm afraid it will break alot of code. Not code in the system so much, but in particular, for personal code of mine' -- an objection about unversioned third-party and personal scripts, which no measurement inside this repository can settle. pzinn also killed the obvious workaround with a real observation: transposing makes the degree shift visible, so 'transpose genericMatrix(...)' prints with a {-1} row label rather than being cosmetically identical. The two live proposals are pzinn's RowMajor option and mahrud's genericMatrix', and mahrud has already said an option is fine. mahrud's second example is a separate instance of the same convention, not covered by either proposal: reshape(R^2, R^3, vars R) also fills column-major. Typed Feature: the behaviour is deliberate and documented by its own consistency, so what is asked for is different functionality, not a defect repair. Labelled Core -- genericMatrix and reshape are both Core scripts.

author: mahrud
title: define applyValues and friends for MutableHashTable
note: Reproduces on 1.26.06-40: applyValues on a MutableHashTable fails with 'expected an immutable hash table'. Nothing implemented. The thread is short and its live question is unanswered. pzinn raised a plausible objection -- 'There might be a technical reason why it's impossible -- e.g., that you can modify the hash table while executing the applyValues, and that would make a mess' -- and pointed at viewHelp scanPairs, which documents that hazard for the immutable case. mahrud's 2025-02-09 reply is the last word and got none: 'The interpreter has facilities to lock the hash table when adding new keys, so what's the technical impossibility?' That is a checkable claim about the interpreter and nobody has checked it, so the issue is blocked on one question that could be settled in an afternoon by whoever knows the locking machinery. author: felixlotter
title: gfanInterface: Another issue with gfanConvertToNewRing
note: Reproduces byte-for-byte on 1.26.06-40: the first maxGrading call returns matrix {{1},{2},{1}}, the second dies with 'no method found for applying promote to: argument 1 : x1 (of class QQ[x1, x2, x3]), argument 2 : R1'. felixlotter's diagnosis is right and the mechanism is narrower than the thread states: TWO SEPARATE DEFECTS SIT IN ONE EXPRESSION, gfanInterface.m2:756-757. (1) The variable names are built as strings and resolved with 'value': 'value ("x" | demark(...) | toString i)'. So if the caller has a global x1, the new ring is built on the CALLER'S symbol rather than a fresh one. (2) That list is handed to '(coefficientRing R1) new Array from (...)', which is Ring Array, and Doug's own comment in the thread quotes it -- polyrings.m2:138, 'Ring Array := PolynomialRing => (R, M) -> use R monoid M' -- so the construction then calls use and rebinds those globals to the new ring. THE FIX IS ALREADY THE FILE'S OWN IDIOM ELSEWHERE: gfanInterface.m2 uses getSymbol in five other places -- :1709 getSymbol("x"), :1803 getSymbol("p"), :1810 getSymbol("m"), :2333 getSymbol("t") and the x|i loop beside it -- and getSymbol is exactly the construct that avoids both problems. So this one function is inconsistent with the rest of its own package. THE USER-SIDE HALF OF THE THREAD ANSWERED ITSELF: felixlotter asked for a local form of use, Doug suggested R monoid M, felixlotter found that leaves the symbols non-variables (which is where #3611's test failure came from), and then found on 2024-12-18 that 'QQ[local x, local y]' gives the scoping he wanted -- with the residual complaint, in his own EDIT, that 'use foo(1)' still leaks. That residual is a separate and much smaller question than the package bug. Typed Bug. Labelled Interfaces: gfanInterface is M2's wrapper around an external program, which is what that label is for, and the defect is in the wrapper rather than in gfan.

author: mahrud
title: Make == a symmetric method
note: Reproduces, but NOT via the example in the body, and I nearly recorded the opposite. mahrud's example uses Vector and ZZ, which have an independent promotion path: on 1.26.06-40 with NOTHING installed, '1 == vector {1}' is already true, '2 == vector {1}' is false, 'vector {1} == 1' is true, and '1 == vector {1,2}' errors -- the error being a promotion failure for a length-2 vector, not a dispatch asymmetry. His own transcript installs his Thing == Thing hack at i2 BEFORE installing Vector == ZZ at i4, so it never isolates whether plain installation suffices. My first reading of that was that == is already symmetric, and a lookup test appeared to confirm it; that test was worthless, because lookup walks ancestors and always finds Thing == Thing, so a non-null result proves nothing. THE CLEAN EXPERIMENT, with fresh types and no built-in path, shows the ask stands exactly as written: 'Foo = new Type of BasicList; Bar = new Type of BasicList;' then installing only 'Foo == Bar' makes 'f == b' run the installed method and leaves 'b == f' erroring with no method found. So == is not symmetric. Neither of mahrud's two proposals exists. The first, his Thing == Thing wrapper comparing lookups in both orders, he calls ugly himself. The second is the substantial one and is unimplemented: reorder the two types by seniority when installing on ==, since the method is always installed on the younger type anyway (his example lands in Vector#(symbol ==, Vector, ZZ)), and teach lookup the same reordering -- generalised to a Symmetric option on 'method'. git grep for Symmetric over m2/methods.m2, d/actors5.d and d/evaluate.d returns nothing. Typed Feature was already correct. Labelled Interpreter: installMethod and lookup are where the reordering would go.

author: mahrud
title: Incorrect ring map evaluation over Weyl algebras
note: Reproduces exactly on 1.26.06-40, all four lines: x_D*dx_D is x*dx, sub(x_D*dx_D, R) is x*dx (good), x_R*dx_R is x*dx, and sub(x_R*dx_R, D) is x*dx+1 (bad). ANTONLEYKIN'S DIAGNOSIS IS CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT, which the thread only conjectured: he guessed 'while creating this map it probably flattened the ring' and offered '(last flattenRing R) (x_R*dx_R)' as the test. Run here it gives dx*x -- the factors reversed -- and in D, dx*x is x*dx+1 by the Weyl relation, which is exactly the wrong answer sub produces. So the corruption enters at the flattening, not in the substitution itself. The thread is a genuine three-way disagreement about scope rather than a stalled bug, and that is why it is open. antonleykin: both sub and map(R,D) should error, since f(dx*x) == f(dx)*f(x) is false, and if not then class f should not be RingMap. moorewf: RingMaps are routinely used for maps that are not well-defined -- map(R,S,gens R) for pulling linear forms back along a surjection -- so erroring would break ordinary practice. antonleykin then proposed a distinct type, SubstitutionMap, with its own contract. mahrud's position is narrower: he does not want a new type, he wants substitute to work between a Weyl algebra and its associated graded ring, and is fine with ring maps erroring. antonleykin's closing question -- what would 'correctly' even mean, and should a literal 'use D; value toString (x_R*dx_R)' be wrapped in a method -- is unanswered. mahrud's aside that sub is a frequent source of inefficiency because it builds a ring map, uses it and discards it, is a separate and unfiled observation. Typed Bug: whatever the design answer, sub returning x*dx+1 for x*dx is wrong. WeylAlgebras label already present.

author: mahrud
title: New top-level mode for LaTeX, HTML, or Org-mode output
note: Stands, all four modes. Nothing in the tree provides a truncated-HTML mode, a LaTeX-source mode, an Org-mode mode or a Markdown mode driven from the plain M2 binary. THE THREAD IS A CLEAN CASE OF TALKING PAST EACH OTHER, and that is the whole of why it is unresolved rather than any technical obstacle. pzinn answered with two existing things: Macaulay2Web run in local mode for the HTTP half, and the TeX mode plus the MergeTeX package for the LaTeX half. mahrud rejected both on the same ground each time -- not that they do not work, but that they are not in the M2 binary: 'Macaulay2Web is an entirely different project, not distributed with M2. If you can embed it in M2 itself so I can run M2 --web that would be great', and 'here I'm asking for something with zero dependencies. Only whatever comes with M2.' His analogy is the clearest statement of the ask: 'Try running python3 -m http.server and imagine instead of the contents of your directory you see the output of an M2 session.' The exchange then went to whether npm is a burden and whether Macaulay2Web needs docker, and pzinn's last word, 2025-04-25, is 'for the record, there's no jquery in Macaulay2Web' -- a correction to a detail, four months after the substance stopped. So no dependency-free top-level mode is being worked on and nobody has disagreed that it would be useful. Typed Feature was already correct. Labelled Core: top-level output modes live with the interpreter's print path, and mahrud's parenthetical question -- whether an M2 thread can interrupt a running command in the main thread -- is the only part that reaches further, into threads. Doug is credited in the body with a usable Org-mode version already.

author: mahrud
title: trim Ideal doesn't trim all the way
note: Reproduces, and the sharp statement is that TRIM IS NOT IDEMPOTENT ON IDEALS. Measured on 1.26.06-40 with the non-graded version: trim I gives 7 generators, ideal(Z-1,Y-1,X-1,x-y,y^2,x*y,x^2); trim of that gives 5, ideal(Z-1,Y-1,X-1,x-y,y^2); trim again stays at 5. So a fixed point is reached on the second pass, and the first answer is mathematically correct -- T1 == T2 is true -- but not minimal. That is the whole defect, and it is why Nick Addington's original report and mahrud's non-graded restatement both work by applying trim twice. The cached run's 'differs at 60%' is an oo artifact: the transcript chains 'trim oo' and the replay's offsets slip, not a behaviour change. NOT A DUPLICATE, and this needed measuring rather than reading, because the vocabulary scores put four trim issues above 0.6. #1012 (DanGrayson, 2019, 'trim doesn't trim enough') is the dangerous one -- older, and the title says the same thing in English. It is a different defect: measured here, its example 'coker matrix {{x,x^2,0},{0,0,1}}' over QQ[x] gives the SAME presentation from trim and trim-trim, so trim is idempotent there and Dan's complaint is that the fixed point it reaches is isomorphic to a simpler module. Non-idempotence on ideals versus a non-minimal fixed point on modules. #747 (naddington, 2018, retitled 'trim over ZZ[x] returns a strictly smaller ideal', commented by this project 2026-08-15) is worse and different again -- a wrong answer over ZZ rather than a non-minimal one over a field. #4095 'trim fails in ZZ[x]' is in that same ZZ family. #1273, which mahrud cites as related, is CLOSED: '(trim, Ideal) should work correctly in single variable polynomial rings'. Typed Bug. Labelled Core: trim on ideals is a Core script.

author: aalmousa
title: syz(Matrix) returns nonminimal syzygies
note: Reproduces exactly on 1.26.06-40, byte for byte with the report: syz h returns a 2x2 matrix whose second column, x^3+x^2+x+1 over -x^4-x^3-x-1, is redundant, and mingens image of it returns a single column. So the documentation for syz(Matrix) -- 'the matrix of minimal or trimmed generators for the syzygies among the columns of h' -- is false as written. aalmousa framed the choice correctly and mikestillman answered it in the thread: 'I think we should fix the documentation.' That is a decision, so what is left is only the wording, and nobody has written it. Two things in Mike's reply are worth not losing. He is unsure what minimality should even mean here -- 'In these instances, I'm not sure what the mathematical notion is for minimality' -- which is the reason the doc cannot simply be tightened to a promise. And he offers a cheap partial improvement rather than a full one: 'during syzygy accumulation, the program could just choose not to append elements which are an obvious multiple of one of the previous ones', which is exactly this example, where the second column is a polynomial multiple of the first. The reporter also identified the internal inconsistency that makes this a documentation bug rather than a code bug: syz(GroebnerBasis) already documents that its output may include nonminimal syzygies, while syz(Matrix) promises the opposite. Typed Bug -- a doc node asserting something false is a defect -- and labelled Documentation, which is where the agreed fix lands. Related, not a duplicate: #4015 'calling mingens after syz gb' and #3017, which the body cites as the origin of the example.

author: d-torrance
title: Several tests running out of memory on i386 when compiling with gcc-14
note: Cannot be tested here and the ask stands. This is i386, a 32-bit architecture, on a 64-bit machine, so the run classification should be read as n/a-platform. THE DEBIAN SIDE IS CLOSED, BY SKIPPING, WHICH IS NOT THE SAME AS FIXED. Debian bug #1095290 is marked severity serious, Found in macaulay2/1.24.11+ds-3, Fixed in 1.24.11+ds-4, Done. The changelog says what the fix was: debian/patches/skip-failing-package-tests.patch, 'Skip several package tests that were blocking the gcc-14 migration (Closes: #1095290)' -- check(5, "LLLBases"), check(15, "PhylogeneticTrees"), check(1, "SparseResultants"), all three annotated 'out of memory on i386', plus check(85, "Complexes") for an s390x timing mismatch. So the three tests named in this issue are the three that were switched off. The very next upload, 1.24.11+ds-5 the following day, added a fourth: check(16, "PhylogeneticTrees"), also 'out of memory on i386'. Nothing addressed the memory use itself. AND THIS ROW IS ITS OWN INSTANCE OF THE REFERENCE-BUILD TRAP: the M2 this project tests against carries those very patches. Grepping the installed packages shows LLLBases with both no-check-flag and 'no-check-architecture: i686', PhylogeneticTrees with two 'no-check-architecture: i686' markers, and SparseResultants with 'no-check-architecture: i686' plus no-check-flag. Upstream, only LLLBases.m2 carries any no-check marker at all; the i686 skips are Doug's packaging. So even on an i386 box, 'check' against this build would establish nothing about these tests, because they are the ones patched out -- the bodies would have to be extracted and run directly, as the README describes for the blanket-skipped rows. author: Devlin-Mallory
title: Reporting infinite projective dimension
note: Reproduces, and the implementation has been REPLACED since the issue was filed, so the premise has moved. The body quotes 'pdim Module := M -> length resolution minimalPresentation M'. That definition is gone. m2/betti.m2:241 now stubs it out -- pdim Module := M -> missingPackage "either Complexes or OldChainComplexes" -- and the live one is Complexes/ChainComplex.m2:638: 'pdim Module := M -> length freeResolution liftModule minimalPresentation M'. The liftModule (m2/pushforward.m2:258, exported at Complexes.m2:94) is the 'computes it over the ambient polynomial ring' behaviour mikestillman flagged on 2026-06-01. MEASURED, AND IT IS SHARPER THAN THE ISSUE ARGUES. Devlin-Mallory's case is that pdim always reports at most dim S + 1 because that is resolution's default LengthLimit, so the bound itself signals infinity. The current implementation does not even respect that bound: with S = QQ[x,y,z], R = S/(x^2) and M = R/(x), pdim M returns 1, while freeResolution(M, LengthLimit => 6) over R has betti 1 in every homological degree 0 through 6 -- periodic, so the projective dimension over R is plainly infinite. pdim says 1. THE DOCUMENTATION IS WORSE THAN UNDOCUMENTED. Mike said the ambient-ring behaviour 'is not documented'; in fact Macaulay2Doc/functions/pdim-doc.m2 asserts the opposite. It is marked 'status: DRAFT', authors L.Gold, Josephine, Jonah; the (pdim, Module) node is headlined 'compute the projective dimension of a module', its Outputs block says ZZ 'the projective dimension', and its only example is over QQ[x,y,z], a polynomial ring, where lifting is a no-op and the divergence never shows. The Caveat on the pdim node -- 'For now, the method is to measure the length of a projective resolution' -- describes the old implementation. There is no pdim doc node in Complexes at all; the only pdim occurrences in ChainComplexDoc.m2 are 'pdim betti C0' inside an example. WHERE THE THREAD LANDED: mahrud's 2026-06-01 reply is the useful one -- 'the change to compute pdim over the ambient polynomial ring wasn't meant to be permanent. I would be in favor of Devlin's suggestion instead of the current behavior' -- so Devlin's proposal now has two maintainers behind it and is the remedy rather than a competing idea. Typed Bug rather than Feature: returning a finite number for a module of infinite projective dimension, under a doc node that promises the projective dimension and an Outputs of ZZ, is a defect; Devlin's infinity is the fix. Related, not duplicates: #3166 (mahrud's, LengthLimit in Complexes, which he cites), #3356 (pdim gives different answers for two generating sets of one module) and #936 (pdim disagreeing with a textbook). Labelled Core -- pdim is core functionality even though its definition now sits in the Complexes package.

author: mahrud
title: big modules printed in error messages
note: Reproduces, with a control that isolates it. Raising the SAME error -- an undefined symbol applied to a matrix -- costs 0.00066s on a 5x5 matrix and 3.00s on a 3000x3000 one over ZZ/32003, a 4500x difference for identical code. Both were wrapped in 'try ... else' AS MY CONTROL, to time the raise without paying to print it -- mahrud's own report has no try in it at all: 'ranks M' is a top-level typo whose error IS printed, as is his 2026-06-11 follow-up, FEED'ME'RAM map(kk^100000, kk^100000, 1) at the prompt. What the control shows is that the object is formatted at raise time rather than print time. MECHANISM, and the 3.00s is a timeout expiring rather than work. m2/methods.m2:22-23, printArgs, calls silentRobustNetWithClass(60, 5, 3, arg), reaching silentRobustNet at m2/robust.m2:35-41: 'truncNet(wid, ht, try timelimit (sec, () -> checkNet ... net y) else (alarm 0; simpleToString y))' with sec = 3, wid = 60, ht = 5. So it renders the WHOLE object with net under a three-second limit and only then truncates to 60 columns and 5 rows. Two consequences for a fix: the truncation happens after formatting rather than during, and the guard is a timeout rather than a size check, so every large operand costs the full three seconds. mahrud's proposed errorPrint would address it; so would consulting the object's dimensions before calling net. The machinery he asks for partly exists, in the wrong order. #3848 IS NOT A DUPLICATE -- comparison done in batch 66, which Doug asked for when that row came up. The two overlap only on 'try plus a big object', and Doug's open PR #4588 separates them inside one file: it skips robustPrintNetWithTab when SuppressErrors is set, which is #3848's ask, but robustPrintNetWithTab reaches Thing.RobustPrintNetMethod = obj -> try silentRobustNetWithClass(60, 5, 3, obj) at robust.m2:62, so a TOP-LEVEL 'bar + baz' on a huge matrix still renders the whole object before truncating to 60x5 and costs after #4588 what it costs now. Its body also says it does not touch the method-function errors in methods.m2, where THIS row's reproducer lives, but the separation does not need that boundary. After it lands they still differ: this row wants a printed message not to render a 3000x3000 matrix before truncating it to 60x5, which is about size and needs no try anywhere; #3848 wants no rendering at all when the message is discarded, which is about try and holds at any size. MEASURED, and it settles the duplicate question against a build where this row's fix has already shipped: KeyNotFound (hashtables.dd:344-350) already carries the 'if !SuppressErrors' guard, added with #3409. On a key whose net, toString and toExternalString each take 10s, that same error costs 3.4e-7s inside a try -- free, the guard works -- and 3.87s against a 0.82s cheap-key baseline at top level with the message printed, a 3.05s delta which is errorPrintingTimeLimit expiring inside silentRobustNetWithClass(60, 5, 3, obj) at robust.m2:62. So this row's fix exists already for one error class and #3661 is fully intact in the same function; #4588 will not change that, since robustPrintNetWithTab -> robustPrintNet -> Thing.RobustPrintNetMethod is robust.m2:62, untouched. No comment on either row.

author: mahrud
title: maximum pipe buffer size
note: Reproduces: the claim is still in the documentation and it is wrong. Macaulay2Doc/ov_files.m2:408 still says 'the buffers associated with the communication channels (pipes) typically hold only 4096 bytes'. Measured through openInOut "!cat" on 1.26.06-40: 65000 bytes written and read back in one round trip, no blocking. Linux's default pipe capacity has been 65536 bytes since kernel 2.6.11 in 2005, and this machine's /proc/sys/fs/pipe-max-size is 1048576, so the figure is two decades stale. mahrud is right that it is outdated. WHAT IS STILL TRUE, AND WHAT THE DOC SHOULD SAY INSTEAD: the general deadlock warning holds -- write more than the pipe holds without reading and you block -- only the number is wrong. And the measurement turned up a behaviour the documentation does not mention at all, which is what a user actually trips over: read returns SHORT. Writing 8000 bytes and asking for 8000 back returned 4096; writing 100000 returned 61248. That is ordinary POSIX behaviour for a pipe, but nothing in the openInOut documentation says a single read may return fewer bytes than requested, and a caller who assumes otherwise will silently lose data rather than block. So the row splits into a stale number, a valid warning, and a missing one. mahrud's actual ask -- 'expand or remove the buffer size limit ... so arbitrarily large amounts can be written/read' -- is a Feature on top of that, and F_SETPIPE_SZ is the mechanism, but the documentation fix stands on its own. Typed Bug because a doc node asserting a false number is a defect. RELATED, not a duplicate: #4594 'openInOut refuses every plain filename, though its documentation offers a named pipe as the example', one of this project's filings, is about the same function's argument handling rather than its buffering.

author: mahrud
title: option Prefix for needsPackage and friends instead of FileName
note: Stands, unimplemented, and the thread stopped on a question. 'options needsPackage' on 1.26.06-40 returns {Configuration, DebuggingMode, FileName, LoadDocumentation, Reload} -- no Prefix -- and git grep finds no Prefix option in m2/packages.m2. mikestillman agreed in the thread on 2025-02-24, 'I would be happy with such a change, I also find it painful to type all that in! Prefix seems like a good solution...', and mahrud's reply the same day was 'Would you like to implement it?'. Nobody answered, and nothing has happened in eighteen months. So this is a small, agreed, unclaimed change rather than a design question: two people who both want it, neither having picked it up.
