author: mahrud
title: `about "Groebner"` vs `about "Gröbner"`
note: Reproduces, and both numbers have moved in the direction that makes it worse. On 1.26.06-40, 'about "Groebner"' returns 86 hits and 'about "Gröbner"' returns 3; the two searches still do not find each other. mahrud saw 85 and 1, so two more nodes now carry the umlaut -- the three are Macaulay2Doc's 'Gröbner bases', 'Gröbner basis algorithms' and 'Tutorial: Elementary uses of Gröbner bases'. That is the drift his ask anticipates: the tree is slowly moving to the correct spelling in titles while the search cannot bridge the two, so each migrated node becomes invisible to the spelling everyone types. His ask is accent-insensitive matching, and nothing implements it. THE TANGENT IS ALSO WORSE, MEASURABLY: 'about("HashTable", Body => true)' returns 24327 hits here against the 21451 he reported, so the useless-result problem has grown by about 2900 nodes in eighteen months. That is a different complaint from the umlaut one -- a search with no relevance ranking over full node bodies -- and it is arguably the more actionable half, since a substring search over every body will only ever get worse as the documentation grows. Typed Feature: neither accent folding nor result ranking exists, so this is missing functionality rather than a defect. Documentation label already present and right.

author: mahrud
title: Disabling XML doesn't work
note: Reproduces as described, and mahrud's diagnosis is exactly right. The option exists: configure.ac:412-415 defines AC_ARG_ENABLE(xml, --disable-xml) and sets WITH_XML accordingly. The cmake side honours it for the FILE LIST -- d/CMakeLists.txt:48 and :83 mark xml.d and xmlactors.d 'removed unless WITH_XML', with the conditional at :102, and :149 makes xml-c.c conditional too. But the TYPE UNION is unguarded: d/parse.d:26 does 'use xml;' and :422 puts 'xmlNodeCell or xmlAttrCell or' in the definition of Expr, with no WITH_XML conditional anywhere in d/*.d -- git grep for WITH_XML over that directory returns only CMakeLists.txt and xml-c.c. So a --disable-xml build removes the file that defines those cells while parse.d still names them, which is precisely the body's 'the definition of Expr in parse.d includes a couple of XML pointer types'. The fix is the pattern already applied one level up: the same conditional the build uses to drop xml.d needs to reach the Expr union and whatever else references those two cells. I did NOT attempt a --disable-xml build to confirm the failure mode, so the claim here is about the source rather than about an observed compile error; that would need a full reconfigure. Typed Bug -- a documented configure option that cannot produce a working build is a defect -- and labelled build issue, which is what that label is for. mahrud's motivation, avoiding XML linkage headaches in the brew build, is unaddressed either way. Zero comments in seventeen months.

author: d-torrance
title: Fix isCyclic MixedGraph
note: Reproduces, and the question the issue asks -- 'it would be good to decide exactly what the behavior should be' -- turns out to be already answered in writing, by the function's own documentation, which the code contradicts. THE TEST IS STILL DISABLED. StatGraphs.m2:1517-1524 carries '-- no-check-flag (see discussion at https://github.com/Macaulay2/M2/pull/3628)' as its first line, so captureTestResult skips it on every architecture. This is one of the three UPSTREAM blanket no-check markers, as distinct from Doug's packaging patches. Running the body directly on 1.26.06-40: isCyclic G is true, so the assertion 'not isCyclic G' fails, which is why it was switched off. The directed part alone is acyclic -- isCyclic D is false for D = digraph{{2,1},{3,1},{7,8}} -- so the true comes from the undirected/bidirected handling. THE DOCUMENTATION SAYS WHAT IT SHOULD BE. The doc node for (isCyclic, MixedGraph) is headlined 'check whether a mixed graph contains a directed cycle' and defines the semantics precisely: 'A directed cycle is a cycle in the Digraph constructed from a mixed graph G by identifying all connected components on bidirected and undirected edges.' And its FIRST EXAMPLE IS THE SAME GRAPH AS THE DISABLED TEST, introduced by the sentence 'In the following example, there are no directed cycles.' THE SHIPPED PAGE THEREFORE CONTRADICTS ITSELF: the example output in /usr/share/doc/Macaulay2/StatGraphs/example-output/_is__Cyclic_lp__Mixed__Graph_rp.out reads 'o5 = true' directly under that sentence, and all four of the node's examples return true, including the one the prose says has none. So the disabled test and the documentation prose agree with each other, and the implementation disagrees with both -- which makes this a defect in isCyclic MixedGraph (StatGraphs.m2:253-274, which contracts components into an adjacency matrix and calls isCyclic on the resulting digraph) rather than an open design question. Whoever picks it up should also fix the garbled comment at :252, 'Check whether a MixedGraph is cyclic, i.e., does not contain any directed cycles'. Typed Bug rather than the suggested Feature: the code contradicts its own documented contract. Labelled package issue -- StatGraphs is a distributed package. #3626 and its fix #3628 are both closed.

author: mahrud
title: sorting bags changes order
note: Reproduces, and the behaviour is sharper than 'changes order': SORT REVERSES. On 1.26.06-40, 'last \ sort \\ Bag \ {{2},{3}}' gives {3,2} as reported; the converse input {{3},{2}} gives {2,3}; and three bags {{1},{2},{3}} give {3,2,1}. So with every comparison returning incomparable -- which is the whole point of 'Bag ? Bag := (x,y) -> incomparable', confirmed here -- sort is not merely reordering unpredictably, it is inverting. A stable sort on mutually incomparable elements would be the identity, so this is a stability failure in sort rather than anything specific to Bag, and Bag is simply the cleanest way to observe it since it is the one type defined to be incomparable with itself. That reframes the fix: the question is not what Bag should do but whether sort is stable when the comparison returns incomparable. Typed Bug: reversing is not a defensible answer for any comparison function. Labelled Core -- Bag and sort are both Core. RELATED, and pzinn's pointer is apt: #650 'Sets don't sort consistently' (open) is the same underlying complaint about a different incomparable-element type, so a fix to sort's handling of incomparable would likely settle both. Not a duplicate -- different types, and #650 is about sets of sets rather than about Bag.

author: aalmousa
title: StopWithMinimalGenerators stops gb computation too early
note: Reproduces exactly, byte for byte with the report, on 1.26.06-40: for R = QQ[x] and H = matrix{{1,0},{x,1+x}}, 'generators gb(H, StopWithMinimalGenerators => true)' returns the single column matrix{{-1},{1}} while 'gens gb H' returns matrix{{-1, x+1},{1, 0}}. So the option drops a generator that the unrestricted computation keeps. THE DOCUMENTATION CANNOT ADJUDICATE IT, WHICH IS WORTH KNOWING BEFORE ANYONE TRIES: the only prose describing this option in Macaulay2Doc is COMMENTED OUT. ov_ringmaps.m2:491-499 carries the whole node behind '--', including the sentence that would settle the question -- 'specifies that the computation should stop as soon as a complete list of minimal generators for the submodule or ideal has been determined' -- and it points at '[gb, StopWithMinimalGenerators]' 'for details', a node that the commented-out block is the only trace of. So a user meeting this option has nothing to read, and the reporters had no written contract to check the behaviour against. That is the first thing to fix regardless of what the engine should do. Typed Bug on the reporters' framing, which two people arrived at together -- aalmousa found it with antonleykin -- and because dropping a generator is not a defensible stopping condition under any reading of the name. Labelled Engine: the option is passed through to the gb computation, which is engine code. Zero comments in sixteen months.

author: mahrud
title: inverse of matrix is not well defined
note: Reproduces exactly, and Devlin-Mallory's diagnosis is confirmed by measurement rather than left as a suspicion. On 1.26.06-40 from the body's own code: 'isWellDefined g and isSurjective g' is true, '(g * inverse g) == id_(target g)' is true, 'isWellDefined inverse g' is FALSE, and 'isWellDefined (id_(target g) // g)' is true. He wrote 'In your example, inverse g is the same matrix as inverse cover g, so I suspect it's essentially treating g as a map of free modules' -- measured, 'matrix inverse g == matrix inverse cover g' is TRUE. THE CAVEAT IS WRITTEN IN THE SOURCE AND NOTHING ENFORCES IT. inverse Matrix (m2/matrix1.m2:624-630) falls through to 'quotientRemainder(id_(target m), m)' whenever the engine's linear algebra does not apply, and quotientRemainder(Matrix,Matrix) opens at m2/matrix2.m2:358-359 with exactly the line he quoted: 'L := source f; -- result may not be well defined if L is not free'. Then :366 does 'f = matrix f', discarding the module structure, which is why the answer coincides with inverse cover g. So the hazard is documented one line into the function inverse depends on, and inverse neither checks for it nor warns. The fix is a guard -- error or warn when the target is not free -- or documenting that 'id_(target g) // g' is the route, which mahrud had already found works and which is slower for the reason the caveat implies. THE THREAD'S SIDE QUESTION IS SETTLED and should not be mistaken for open: mahrud proposed 'g \\ id_(source g)' as an alternative and got zero; Devlin-Mallory explained that asks for a LEFT inverse, which cannot exist for a surjection with nontrivial kernel, and mahrud accepted it -- 'Ah, of course, I drew my diagram wrong'. He also noted 'the original issue still stands', which is this. Devlin-Mallory's general caution is worth keeping too: isWellDefined and isSurjective together only imply invertibility when the target is projective. No comment: he diagnosed it correctly and the additions are line numbers. Typed Bug and labelled Core -- inverse, quotientRemainder and // are all Core scripts. RELATED, none a duplicate: #4506 'inverse of a non-square matrix returns a matrix', #4556 'inverse of a singular matrix over RR or CC', #3973 'Internal error inverting element of tower ring'.

author: mahrud
title: debug(Package) should enable debugging mode for the package
note: Stands, unimplemented, zero comments in sixteen months. Measured on 1.26.06-40: 'debug Package' exists -- methods debug are (debug,ZZ), (debug,String), (debug,Package), (debug,LocalDictionary), (debug,GlobalDictionary) -- but it does not touch debugging mode. After 'debug Text', debuggingMode is still false and (options Text).DebuggingMode is still false. What debug Package does today is open the package's private dictionary so unexported symbols become visible; mahrud's ask is that it ALSO turn on debugging for that package, so errors from it get more depth without setting errorDepth globally, which is the workaround he names in the body. Worth flagging for whoever implements it that this is not just a one-line addition to debug: DebuggingMode is a newPackage option consulted at load time, so making it per-package and settable afterwards is the actual work, and error depth is currently a single global. Typed Feature was already correct. Labelled Core -- debug, debuggingMode and errorDepth are all Core.

author: mahrud
title: documentation of Degree of a map
note: Reproduces, and mahrud is right in the plain reading rather than only under a charitable one. The sentence is still at Macaulay2Doc/functions/map-doc.m2:213-214: 'For example, multiplication of a matrix by a scalar increases the degree, leaving the source and target fixed'. Measured on 1.26.06-40 with R = QQ[x,y] and m = matrix{{x,y}}: degree m is {0}, degree(2*m) is {0}, degree(2_R*m) is {0}, and degree(x*m) is {1}. So a scalar does NOT increase the degree, whether taken in the coefficient ring or promoted into R; a ring element of positive degree does. THE DOC'S OWN EXAMPLE ALREADY DEMONSTRATES THE CORRECT STATEMENT, which nobody in the thread noticed: the EXAMPLE block immediately under that sentence is 'R = QQ[a,b]; f1 = matrix{{a,b}}; f = a * f1; degree f', i.e. multiplication by the VARIABLE a, not by a scalar. So the prose is simply mislabelling what the code beneath it does, and Devlin-Mallory's proposed wording -- 'multiplication of a matrix by a ring element of positive degree increases the degree' -- matches the existing example exactly. That makes it a one-word documentation fix with an agreed replacement and a worked example already in place. Devlin-Mallory's charitable reading, that 'scalar' was intended to mean an element of ring M rather than of coefficientRing M, is a fair guess at intent but the measurement shows the sentence is false as written under either reading of 'scalar' in ordinary usage. mahrud's broader remark -- 'that's a subtle page that should be documented better' -- is open-ended and not settled by the one-word fix. Typed Bug: a doc node asserting something false is a defect. Documentation label already present.

author: mahrud
title: Complexes transition issues tracker
note: Stands as a tracker, and it is doing its job -- two of five items are checked and the three open ones are all still open, verified on 1.26.06-40. UNCHECKED AND CONFIRMED OPEN. author: mahrud
title: TopDirectory in Bertini
note: Reproduces, and the shipped documentation demonstrates it. The installed page /usr/share/doc/Macaulay2/Bertini/html/_bertini__User__Homotopy.html reads 'TopDirectory => ..., default value "/tmp/M2-41494-0/0"' -- a build-time temporary directory baked into the released documentation. mahrud saw '/tmp/M2-2629113-0/0'; the digits differ because they are whatever process id the documentation build happened to use, which is the point: every build ships a different string, and it names a path that does not exist on the reader's machine. MECHANISM, as the body says: Bertini.m2 fixes globals at load time (the lines mahrud links, around :202-214) and then uses storeBM2Files as the default VALUE of an option rather than as a default computed at call time, so the value is captured when the documentation is generated. storeBM2Files appears 56 times in the installed Bertini.m2, so this is the package's pervasive idiom rather than one slip. antonleykin agreed on 2025-05-08 -- 'we should avoid documentation mutation without necessity' -- and added @JoseMath; nothing since. Worth noting the general shape for whoever fixes it: an option whose default is a mutable global will always leak the build environment into the docs, so the fix is to make the default a symbol resolved at call time, not to change what the global is set to. Typed Bug: shipping a nonexistent /tmp path as a documented default is wrong, even if harmless. Labelled Interfaces, which is what the tier-1 suggester matched and is right -- Bertini is M2's wrapper around an external solver.

author: tom111
title: `isRegularSequence` from `Depth` package does not work in multigraded setting
note: Reproduces, and the mechanism is two expressions on one line. Depth.m2:267-269 sets T := (degreesRing ring M)_0 and tests the Hilbert-series identity against product(X, i -> 1 - T^(first degree i)): 'first degree' collapses a multidegree to its first component, so in QQ[x,y, Degrees=>{{1,0},{0,1}}] the factor for y is 1 - T_0^0 = 0, the product is 0, and the equality fails against a left side of 1 - T_0 - T_1 + T_0*T_1. Substituting D_(degree i) -- the multidegree monomial in the whole degrees ring -- for T^(first degree i) returns true for {x,y}, and still false for {x,x*y} and for {x,y} over R/(x*y); the standard-graded branch is untouched because degree is a one-element list there, checked on QQ[a,b,c] both ways. The multigraded ring reaches the homogeneous branch, so the else branch's regularSequenceCheck is never consulted.

(2) The mechanism is being fixed for operator errors by Doug's open PR #4588, which moves 'no method found' for unary/binary operators into the interpreter and writes exactly what this issue asks: 'if !SuppressErrors then msg = msg + " to:" + robustPrintNetWithTab(x)' in evaluate.d, where SuppressErrors is the flag tryEval sets (evaluate.d:1305). It also deletes the robust.m2 block that installed the Thing op Thing fallbacks calling silentRobustNetWithClass(wid, ht, errorPrintingTimeLimit, x). Measured on the reference build before that lands: an object whose net, toString and toExternalString each take 10s costs 'try (x == null) else ...' exactly 3.00s, which is errorPrintingTimeLimit in m2/robust.m2:10 -- and == is one of the flexibleBinaryOperators whose fallback #4588 removes, so this number should go to zero. (3) What stands is the general form: error still builds its message at raise time for everything else -- errorfun (d/debugging.dd:295) calls processErrorArgs0, which calls robustPrintString on every non-string argument with no reference to SuppressErrors -- plus the tests mahrud asked for. Part 2 of his ask was already deferred to #3638. NOT A DUPLICATE OF #3661, and #4588 is the demonstration, in one file: it skips robustPrintNetWithTab when SuppressErrors, which is this row's ask, but robustPrintNetWithTab reaches Thing.RobustPrintNetMethod = obj -> try silentRobustNetWithClass(60, 5, 3, obj) at robust.m2:62, still rendering the whole object before truncating to 60x5 under the 3s timeout -- so a TOP-LEVEL 'bar + baz' on a huge matrix costs after #4588 exactly what it costs now, which is #3661. It also leaves methods.m2 alone, where #3661's own reproducer lives, but the separation does not need that boundary. They would still differ afterwards -- #3661 wants a printed message not to render a 3000x3000 matrix before truncating it to 60x5, which is about size and needs no try; this row wants no rendering at all when the message is discarded, which is about try and holds at any size. MEASURED, and it settles the duplicate question against a build where this row's fix has already shipped: KeyNotFound (hashtables.dd:344-350) already carries the 'if !SuppressErrors' guard, added with #3409. On a key whose net, toString and toExternalString each take 10s, that same error costs 3.4e-7s inside a try -- free, the guard works -- and 3.87s against a 0.82s cheap-key baseline at top level with the message printed, a 3.05s delta which is errorPrintingTimeLimit expiring inside silentRobustNetWithClass(60, 5, 3, obj) at robust.m2:62. So this row's fix exists already for one error class and #3661 is fully intact in the same function; #4588 will not change that, since robustPrintNetWithTab -> robustPrintNet -> Thing.RobustPrintNetMethod is robust.m2:62, untouched.

author: jkyang92
title: isVeryAmple is incorrect for Polyhedrons
note: Reproduces exactly on 1.26.06-40: isVeryAmple P returns true while the Hilbert basis of the tangent cone at (1,0,0) contains (0,2,1), which is not in P minus that vertex, so P is not very ample. MECHANISM LOCATED, one line: Polyhedra/extended/polyhedron/properties.m2:34, 'ind == 1 or (...)'. The test builds the primitive outgoing-edge directions at each vertex, takes the product of the Smith normal form elementary divisors, and accepts the vertex if that product is 1. Sound only at a SIMPLE vertex, where #edges == dim P and the edge directions are a basis of the tangent cone, so ind==1 means the cone is unimodular. At a non-simple vertex the directions can generate Z^n as a LATTICE (ind==1) while the cone they generate is not smooth. Instrumented the loop: all six vertices of P have ind==1, and (1,0,0) has FIVE outgoing edges in ambient dimension 3, so the shortcut fires and both remaining branches are skipped -- and both evaluate to FALSE when run by hand. Of the six Hilbert basis elements, five lie in P-v and (0,2,1) is the single failure, exactly the vector the reporter named. Gating on '#outgoingEdges == dim P and ind == 1' returns false on this P and still true on the unit simplex; have NOT measured that against the package test suite, so it is a diagnosis not a patch. Shortcut dates to 2c4338389d (Rene Birkner, 2010-01-10), the commit that added isVeryAmple, untouched since -- not a regression. NOT A DUPLICATE of #3575 (isVeryAmple ToricDivisor in NormalToricVarieties, fix in PR #3582); that row's note already recorded this one as related. Label 'package issue' not NormalToricVarieties -- the suggester matched 'ToricDivisor' from the reporter's closing aside, but the defect is in Polyhedra.

author: mahrud
title: strict equality of complexes
note: Every claim in the thread reproduces on 1.26.06-40: complex R === complex R is false, canonicalTruncation(C,(1,1)) === itself is false, C === C[1][1][-2] is false, complex(C[1], Base => 0) === C is false, and mahrud's // failure comes back with the exact error -- expected targets of two maps to be the same complex, at Complexes/ChainComplexMap.m2:1286 -- while target f' == target g' is true on the same two objects. Both halves are live: Complex inherits from MutableHashTable, === is therefore object identity, and methods that rebuild a complex from the same input hand back a different object. ggsmith settled the direction in-thread on 2025-06-05 and called it a bug: canonicalTruncation should cache so identical input gives identical output, and the =!= in liftMapAlongQuasiIsomorphism should stay because == on complexes is expensive. mahrud's 2025-07-15 follow-up is the unanswered part -- shifts make caching insufficient on its own, since C === C[1][1][-2] would need all shifts to share one representation. NO DUPLICATE among open issues: his own earlier #3865 and #3875 are both closed, and #3608 (make == a symmetric method) is about dispatch, not identity. n-m-g's SpectralSequences PR #3807 line was ruled out by mahrud in-thread. author: mahrud
title: equality of elements of submodules of the same module
note: Both halves reproduce on 1.26.06-40: M_0 == N_1 is false while M_{0} == N_{1} is true, and set M_* == set N_* is false while the corresponding set of images is true, exactly as posted. author: mahrud
title: Interrupting Normaliz crashes M2
note: DID NOT REPRODUCE the abort, and the reason is located, so this is not a not-reproducible row. Attempt: rawHilbertBasis on a 14x5 nonnegative random matrix takes 36s here; SIGINT at 10s, squarely inside libnormaliz, gives a clean 'interrupted, stopping' and exit 2. No InterruptException, no abort. WHY IT CANNOT FIRE ON THIS BUILD: libnormaliz raises InterruptException only from INTERRUPT_COMPUTATION_BY_EXCEPTION (general.h:113), which tests libnormaliz::nmz_interrupted, and that flag is set only by libnormaliz::interrupt_signal_handler. Checked the Normaliz repo at both v3.8.9 and v3.11.1: that handler is installed in exactly one place, source/normaliz.cpp:182, the command-line driver -- never by the library. An embedding application must install it itself, and M2 does not; nmz_interrupted and interrupt_signal_handler appear nowhere in the M2 tree, and M2 installs its own SIGINT handler at Macaulay2/d/M2lib.c:25. BUT THE DEFECT IS REAL AND PRESENT, which is why this stands: if the exception is ever thrown, nothing catches it. libnormaliz::InterruptException derives from NormalizException : public std::exception, NOT from std::runtime_error, and Macaulay2/e/interface/cone.cpp catches only exc::engine_error (62 rawFourierMotzkin, 103 rawHilbertBasis, 380 rawConeInteriorPoint) and std::runtime_error (263, 321). So it escapes every try block to std::terminate and abort() -- exit 134 with 'terminate called after throwing an instance of libnormaliz::InterruptException', the transcript in the body verbatim. THE CONTROL IS NOT VALID and that is worth being explicit about: this build links Debian libnormaliz 3.8.9, while M2's own cmake build fetches 3.11.1 (cmake/build-libraries.cmake:975) and mahrud's transcript is from a linuxbrew cmake build. Cannot say from here how his process came to have nmz_interrupted set; that is the one open question and only he can answer it. Engine because the fix site is e/interface/cone.cpp; Interfaces because the subject is the linked external library.

author: kschwede
title: pushFwd incorrect behavior on certain rings produced by flattenRing
note: Reproduces exactly on 1.26.06-40: prune myMod is QQ^2 where it must be QQ^6, and myFun(x) dies with 'rawFreeModule: degree rank 0, but sequence of degrees given'. CORRECTION OWED on the comment published under Doug's account 2026-08-06 (source comments/bugs/dan/1-flattenRing.md, posted via the bugs/ project under marker bug-triage:bugs/dan/1-flattenRing, so the correction goes out as comments/issues/3887.2.md). Its transcript only ever exercised myFun and never prune myMod, which is kschwede's headline complaint. ONE VARIABLE AT A TIME ON S2 (degree rank 2 AND product order GRevLex/Position=>Up/GRevLex, both changed at once by the workaround): Degrees=>{1,1} alone gives WRONG module QQ^2 but myFun works; MonomialOrder=>GRevLex alone gives CORRECT QQ^6 but myFun still errors; both gives QQ^6 and working myFun. So on this ring the module rank is controlled by the MONOMIAL ORDER and the degree-rank-0 error by the DEGREE RANK. SCOPE THAT TO THIS RING -- do not generalise, the trap I nearly walked into twice and which Doug caught by asking about #3284. On #3284's OWN body ring, where degree rank is the only difference and both rings carry a single GRevLex block, R = QQ[x,y,Degrees=>{{1,0},{0,1}}]/(x^3-2,y^2+y+1) ERRORS on pushFwd(map(R,QQ[])) while singly graded S returns (QQ[])^6. So degree rank alone does break a case -- the QQ[] source case -- it just is not what costs you the rank. Also: kschwede's 'wrong answer if the source is QQ' does NOT reproduce; both rings give QQ^6 for source QQ on 1.26.06-40. NOT A DUPLICATE of #3284 (2024-06-05, older, labelled Core), and the reason is sharper than 'close but not the same': every ring in #3284's BODY carries a single GRevLex block, so the product-order fault behind this issue's wrong module is not exhibited there at all. The overlap is via Claudiu Raicu's minimal example in #3284's COMMENTS, which does use flattenRing and does share the monomial-order cause -- verified: on it, degrees-only still returns a rank-4 kernel and order-only returns image 0. Closing this into #3284 would fold a monomial-order bug into an issue whose title and body are about multigraded degree rank, and would lose the degree-rank myFun symptom #3284 does not have. author: mahrud
title: overwriting pi
note: Stands. pi is a protected global defined at m2/reals.m2:371, pi = new Constant from { symbol pi, pi0, piRRi0 }, and pi = 3 is refused with 'assignment to protected global variable pi, originally defined at Core/reals.m2:371'. author: mahrud
title: freeResolution and syz are not thread-safe
note: BOTH halves reproduce verbatim on 1.26.06-40. freeResolution: two scheduled tasks on truncate(5, S^1) give 'error: key not found in hash table: isComputable (of class Symbol)' at Complexes/FreeResolution.m2:91 and 'class \\ oo' returns {Complex, Nothing} -- mahrud's transcript exactly, down to the second task returning Nothing. (His path said FreeResolutions.m2:91 on 1.25.06; the file is now FreeResolution.m2, same line, same error.) syz: five scheduled 'syz gens M' gives -- SIGSEGV / -- SIGSEGV handler called a second time, aborting / exit 2, also verbatim. RACE LOCATED for the first half, and it is a publish-before-initialize: FreeResolution.m2:106-112 builds RO with exactly five keys (ring, LengthLimit, DegreeLimit, Strategy, Module), line 113 publishes it with 'M.cache.ResolutionObject = RO', and only then does line 116 call runHooks, whose strategy hooks install RO.isComputable (lines 188, 404, 426, 488, 550). author: d-torrance
title: bug in randomPoints
note: Reproduces, and the mechanism is one line with a valid control. eisenbud reported it loops forever; under --script it surfaces as 'recursion limit of 300 exceeded' within seconds, and raising recursionLimit to 10000 just moves the wall -- it is unbounded recursion, not slow progress. Frame census of the backtrace: RandomPoints.m2:467 appears 77 times. That line is the tail of getRandomLinearForms: 'if (rank J1 < val) then (... return getRandomLinearForms(R1, L1, opts);)' at RandomPoints.m2:461-467, a retry with no bound and no change of strategy. WHY THE GUARD CAN NEVER PASS on this input: with Degrees => {2,1}, basis(1, A2) is matrix {{y}} -- the degree-one piece is spanned by y alone -- so every random(1, A2) is a scalar multiple of y and the Jacobian of any number of such forms has rank 1, while val := min(d, #formList) is 2. So rank J1 < val holds forever. Control: in kk[x,y] with standard degrees basis(1, B2) is {x, y}, the same construction gives Jacobian rank 2, and the guard passes on the first try. The only difference between the two sides is the degree vector, and it is precisely what makes the degree-one graded piece one-dimensional. Plain 'gb I' on the same ring is fine, so this is RandomPoints, not the Groebner engine. That also explains why Homogeneous => false did not help eisenbud: the linear forms still come from random(1, R1). Zero comments since filing in October 2025.

author: mahrud
title: delayed error printing when no method is applicable
note: Reproduces and is severe, but I could not explain it, so it is recorded as a measurement rather than a finding. complex(apply(toList(0..10), i -> M)) takes 0.00009s; dropping the toList so the argument is a Sequence takes 4.77s of cpuTime to reach 'no method found', at only 300x300 -- mahrud used 1000x1000 and said minutes. WHAT IT IS NOT: not proportional to formatting the argument. Cold, in fresh processes, the error path is essentially FLAT in matrix size -- 4.24s at n=100, 4.54s at n=200, 4.63s at n=300 -- while net of the same sequence is steeply superlinear over that range, 6.5s, 37s, 136s. So the error path is not calling net on the argument. It does depend on the elements being nontrivial modules: 11 integers cost 0.00009s and 11 copies of R^1 cost 0.00017s, versus 4.24s for 11 copies of a 100x100 cokernel and 5.04s for 400x400. author: naddington
title: trim fails in ZZ[x]
note: Reproduces, and it is BROADER than the unit ideal and WORSE than the neighbouring trim issues. (a) It is a wrong answer, not a non-minimal one: for I = ideal(x^2+x+1, x^4+x^3+x^2+x+1) in ZZ[x], trim I is ideal(x+1) while T == I is FALSE and 1_R % T is 1 -- x^2+x+1 is not in the result, so trim returned a proper subideal. (b) NOT CONFINED TO THE UNIT IDEAL, which is the framing of the report and of pzinn's workaround: J = ideal(x^2+1, x^3+1) has gens gb J = | 2 x+1 |, so J = ideal(2, x+1), PROPER -- and trim J gives ideal(x-1), dropping the constant and returning a different linear form. So the unit ideal is not the special case and '== 1 first' has nothing to latch onto there. (c) pzinn's ordering effect generalises and the operative step is the GROEBNER BASIS, not '== 1': from freshly constructed ideals, trim gives ideal(x+1), 'I == 1 then trim' gives ideal 1, and 'gens gb I then trim' also gives ideal 1. == just happens to compute a basis. (d) Scope: ZZ[x,y] fails identically (trim == I false); QQ[x] is fine. METHOD NOTE, and it bit me twice: trim caches, so every comparison needs a freshly constructed ideal -- my first check trimmed before testing pzinn's claim and got the wrong answer both times, and my first draft of the comment showed 'gens gb J' immediately before 'trim J', which would have displayed the CORRECT answer and contradicted the point being made. Both fixed before publication. DISTINCT FROM THE TWO CROSS-REFERENCES Doug gave: #3622 is trim not being idempotent, where our own triage found the first answer mathematically CORRECT but not minimal and a second trim reaches a fixed point -- here the first answer is wrong and a second trim cannot recover it. #1273 is closed and correctly so: its example is ZZ/7[t], a PID, its text says 'when working over a PID', PR #3018 fixed that, and trim ideal(t^3*(t+1), t*(t-1)) now gives ideal t. ZZ[x] has Krull dimension 2 and is not a PID.

It then asks about coker(x) over QQ[x,y], dim 1, instead of M3 over R2, dim 0 -- hence false. BTOTARO'S PROPOSED FIX IS WHAT THE CODE ALREADY DOES: he suggests translating to the polynomial ring; that translation is the bug. His other guess is also wrong in a useful way -- the annihilator is computed CORRECTLY and already contains y^2, since y^2 = -x^2 in R2: annihilator M3 is ideal x, y^2 % (ideal x) == 0 is true, isSubset(m^2, ann) is true, radical(ann) == m is true. All three say the answer should be true. (2) PATH 1 IS CORRECT AND USUALLY SKIPPED, which answers his second paragraph, the one he says he does not understand. It returns saturate(annihilator M, B) == ideal 1 -- true here -- but only when isComputationDone container, i.e. when the SATURATION is already cached; otherwise the branch value is discarded and control falls through to path 2. Verified in three separate processes: fresh false, after annihilator M false, after annihilator M AND saturate(N,m) TRUE. So caching the annihilator alone, which is what he tried, cannot help. (3) NEW, UNREPORTED: the function REBINDS THE CALLER'S RING VARIABLES. Building R from (coefficientRing S)[(S_*)_perm, ...] binds the symbols x and y to the new ring's generators, so after one call ring x === R2 goes from true to FALSE and ring x is QQ[x..y]. The next expression using x then fails with 'expected matrices for compatible rings'. I FIRST REPORTED THAT ERROR AS AN UNLOCALISED SECOND FAILURE MODE OF THE FUNCTION AND WAS WRONG; Doug asked me to dig in before deciding on a comment, and it is this shadowing biting the FOLLOWING statement, not the function failing twice. title: bug in decreasing allowableThreads

author: mahrud
title: Crash in parallel gb computations
note: REPRODUCED HERE, which settles the thread's platform question: mahrud's 2026-04-29 snippet (QQ[x_1..x_5], M = coker (res coker vars R).dd_4, apply(10, i -> schedule(poincare, M))) segfaults on 1.26.06-40 in 9 of 54 runs on Linux x86-64 Ubuntu 24.04 -- with mahrud (linux x86) and Devlin-Mallory (macOS M1), against mikestillman's clean M4. SEPARATE FINDING, and the reason nobody can compare traces: on this build the crash handler cannot produce one. Every crash log stops after '-- SIGSEGV' and '-* stack trace, pid: N' with no frames and no '-- end stack trace *-' marker, and two of the six went further -- '-- SIGSEGV / -- SIGSEGV handler called a second time, aborting' -- so segv_handler (bin/main.cpp:233) faults inside boost::stacktrace::stacktrace() and trips its own re-entry guard. That guard, 'static int level', is a plain unsynchronised int: in one log the pid line prints AFTER the abort message, which is two threads inside the handler at once, not one thread re-entering. Exit codes follow: 0 where the handler died silently, 2 down the double-fault path, never the 1 a completed handler would give -- so a crash is invisible to exit-code checks and has to be found by grepping stderr for SIGSEGV. NOT a stripping problem: Doug corrected an earlier version of this note, and he is right -- macaulay2-dbgsym is installed at the matching version, and /usr/lib/debug/.build-id/da/7541b39229750a30fa13e2ae6ead32a7ed3855.debug (52MB) matches M2-binary's build-id, so the symbols are there and the handler still cannot walk the stack. author: mahrud
title: Optimizing overhead of syntactic sweeteners for functions

The SUBSCRIPT pair is the only consistent one: apply(L, blah2_x) is slower than apply(L, y -> blah2(x,y)) in every run, ratios 1.09, 1.21, 1.29, 1.29. COMPOSITION does not hold a direction: 1.04, 1.05, 1.16, then 0.81 at 2M, where each timing is seconds and GC dominates -- so no reliable difference. His intuition is therefore right for _ and unsupported for the other two, and his own pseudocode explains why: blah_x evaluates the 2-OP _ node once and then calls the resulting closure per element, one extra call layer, which predicts exactly a small constant overhead. (1) THE DOLLAR SIGN IS MISSING FROM BOTH PAGES: ctype.d:26 sets ALNUMEXTRA on "$'", so 'a$b = 1' is accepted exactly as x' is. (2) 'should not begin with a digit' is too weak: isvalidsymbol (ctype.d:69) requires isalpha on the first character, so 'x and $x are both REJECTED even though neither begins with a digit. (3) UNICODE LETTERS WORK AND ARE UNDOCUMENTED: ctype.d:28 marks every byte 128-255 ALPHA, so 'α = 1' is accepted. One nuance to be careful about when writing the fix: ctype.d:70-72 makes a lone math operator a valid symbol, but that does not make it assignable -- '⊗ = 1' is rejected, since ⊗ is already an operator token. pzinn's #3599 is offered as the cleanup. note: Cannot be reproduced here -- macOS arm64 with AppleClang, and this machine is Linux -- but the code is a single site and it matches the symptom. cmake/configure.cmake:227-233 is an 'elseif(CMAKE_C_COMPILER_ID STREQUAL AppleClang)' branch containing 'if(CMAKE_OSX_SYSROOT) add_compile_options(--sysroot=${CMAKE_OSX_SYSROOT}) add_link_options(--sysroot=${CMAKE_OSX_SYSROOT}) endif()', and that is the only place M2's cmake emits --sysroot at all, so the bare '--sysroot=' in his link line comes from here with the variable expanding to nothing. His workaround (-DCMAKE_OSX_SYSROOT=macosx) works by giving it a value, which fits. Worth flagging for whoever fixes it: a plain if() would not fire on an empty string, so the interesting question is what CMAKE_OSX_SYSROOT held at configure time on his machine -- and the guard is AppleClang-only, so a Homebrew clang build would never hit it. build issue label already present

author: d-torrance
title: line number not found in file stdio when running "code"
note: Reproduces, and the mechanism explains pzinn's 'somewhat randomly' too. On 1.26.06-40, two identical 'code(() -> return)' lines fed at once give the reported 'error: line number 1 not found in file stdio' on the second. The cause is history indexing, not positions: locate is correct in every case (peek gives FilePosition{stdio,1,...}, {stdio,2,...}, {stdio,3,...} for three successive lines), but with pasted or piped input the WHOLE BLOCK lands in history entry 1 and the rest come back empty -- 'apply(1..4, i -> getHistory(i + historyOffset))' returns the four-line block, then "", "", "". code's stdio branch (m2/code.m2:64-69) rebuilds the source by stacking getHistory over the position's line range, so for anything defined after the first line of a block it stacks an empty string, and the guard at :76 ('if #file < stop then error("line number "...)') fires with 0 < 1. THE PATTERN pzinn could not see is exactly that: any input line after the first in a pasted block, which is every line on Macaulay2Web where input arrives in blocks. #4351 is the trigger rather than the cause -- it gave 'return' a position, so code now attempts a lookup it previously skipped; the history-indexing bug is older and independent. bug and Core labels already present

author: pzinn
title: MutableMatrix multiplication bug
note: Reproduces, worse than reported, and there is a quieter case that is arguably worse still. pzinn's example on 1.26.06-40 gives an entry whose toString is 603662 characters (he saw 65k) and Doug's follow-up holds exactly: 'denominator lift((last coefficients oo_(0,0))_(0,0), QQ)' is 0, a corrupt QQ. The immutable path is correct throughout -- (matrix{{x}})*(matrix{{y}}) is matrix {{x*y}} over the same frac(QQ[x])[y]. NEW AND SMALLER: no frac needed, and no garbage -- in S = QQ[x][y] with use S, 'mutableMatrix{{x}} * mutableMatrix{{y}}' returns x^2 where the immutable product is x*y. The factors show why: ring a_(0,0) is QQ[x], the coefficient ring, while ring b_(0,0) is S, so mutableMatrix is not promoting to a common ring and the product reinterprets one factor's variable as the other's. Three lines, a silently wrong answer, and no 600KB output to hide it in. Engine label already present; dropping the bug label per Doug's standing instruction

author: mahrud
title: negative numbers from minimalBetti
note: Not reproducible sequentially here, and a strong lead for why. Extracted both of mahrud's examples from the comments with gh: the 10-variable ZZ/32003[s_0..s_9, Degrees => {6:1,4:2}] case and the 11-variable one with a degree-3 generator. Both give minimalBetti with ZERO negative entries on 1.26.06-40 -- for the first, all 32 entries positive, total 1 35 160 340 303 173 118 35 1. author: pzinn
title: discriminant throwing an error when it probably shouldn't
note: Reproduces and the chain is short. discriminant is packages/Elimination.m2:128, 'discriminant(f,x) := resultant(f, diff(x,f), x)', and sylvesterMatrix at :108 refuses a zero argument -- 'if f == 0 or g == 0 then error "expected nonzero polynomials"'. pzinn's F has every exponent even (24,22,20,14,12,8,4) so over ZZ/2 its formal derivative is identically zero: diff(x,F) is 0 here, and the ZZ/3 analogue y^6+y^3 does the same. So the error is the resultant guard firing on a legitimately zero derivative, and his generalisation -- any ZZ/p with exponents divisible by p -- is exactly right. Worth noting for whoever fixes it: for an inseparable polynomial the discriminant is 0, not undefined, so the fix is a value rather than a better error message. author: pzinn
title: error multiplying matrices with entries in fraction field
note: Reproduces, and the representations are visible, which settles which of pzinn's two diagnoses is the live one. On 1.26.06-40 with F = frac(QQ[y]): a = matrix{{1/2}}*matrix{{y}} and b = matrix{{y/2}} compare false under == and ===, while a-b == 0 is true. The entries differ in FORM, not value -- (numerator, denominator) is ((1/2)*y, 1) for a and (y, 2) for b. So it is his first problem, the lack of a canonical form: with QQ as the coefficient field a denominator of 2 can live either in the denominator or in the coefficients, and frac does not normalise between them. His second proposal, relaxing equality to ad == bc, would paper over that rather than fix it, and would also be the more invasive of the two at the c level. Nothing else in the thread to settle: mahrud's a-b==0 workaround was already the body's last line and he withdrew the comment himself. Adding Engine -- frac arithmetic is engine-side

author: pzinn
title: non uniqueness of ZZ/n for n nonprime
note: Reproduces, and pzinn's guess is exactly right, down to a single early return. On 1.26.06-40 'ZZ/4 === ZZ/4' is FALSE while 'ZZ/5 === ZZ/5' is true, and binding R = ZZ/4 once gives the expected 'unique' result {0, 1, 2, -1} -- so nothing is wrong with the arithmetic, only with ring identity. The site is m2/quotring.m2:80-84: the constructor memoises in savedQuotients#(typ, n) and consults it first, but before reaching that it does 'if not isPrime n or n > 2^64 then return ZZ[DegreeRank => 0]/n', which builds a fresh ring and never touches the cache. Hence every ZZ/4 is a new object. Worth noting the condition has a second arm: a PRIME larger than 2^64 takes the same early return, so ZZ/p is non-unique there too, not just for composite n. Core label already present; dropping the bug label per Doug's standing instruction

author: tsandstr
title: Documentation for `isHomogeneous(Matrix)` unclear
note: The four answers are all CORRECT, so this is a documentation row rather than a behavior row -- which is what the title says. Re-measured on 1.26.06-40, unchanged from the report: foo homogeneous of degree {1}, bar homogeneous {0}, baz NOT homogeneous with degree {0}, qux homogeneous {0}, and foo == baz, bar == qux both true. The distinction is the third argument: map(M,N,x) with a RingElement absorbs degree x into the degree shift, while map(M,N,matrix x) with a Matrix does not, so baz really is inhomogeneous against its recorded degree {0}. tsandstr's expectation corresponds to an existential reading of homogeneity -- is there SOME shift making this homogeneous -- which M2 does not implement and the doc sentence he quotes does not exclude. Investigated at length on 2026-08-03 against 1.26.06-8; the notes are in ISSUE_4487.md in the checkout root, untracked and unpublished. Beyond the wording, that pass found (degree, Matrix) has no documentation node at all, and that map-doc.m2:183-185's claim 'This gives the same map as r * map(M,N,1)' holds for == but not for isHomogeneous or degree on a non-free module.
